info.description: Every action of the Kadr video editor is available as a command. POST the arguments as JSON to /api/v1/commands/{name}. Times are integers in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A running Kadr writes <data folder>/api-endpoint.json {url, pid, version, token_file, started_at}: read the address from url and the token from token_file (normally <data folder>/api-token). The port is configurable (app.api.set, settings.json "api", KADR_ADDR); the default is 127.0.0.1:7777.
info.title: Kadr Editor API

post.description:
Adds a neutral adjustment layer — a segment on an adjustment track whose colour controls (brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, sharpen, vignette, LUT) apply to everything below it for its time range, like "Custom adjustment" in the Adjustment tab. Placed at at_us (default: playhead) for duration_us (default 3 s). Set the values afterwards with segment.set_adjust on the returned segment.
UI: Library/Adjustment/Custom adjustment.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, track_id, segment} — segment.adjust holds the (neutral) Adjustments.

example1.summary: Adjustment layer for the first 10 s

at_us.description: Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

duration_us.description: Length of the new adjustment segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks.

post.description:
Automatically corrects the colour of a video/photo clip or of an adjustment layer — CapCut's Auto adjust wand. Renders one representative frame (by default the middle of the segment; time_us picks another moment) of what the segment colours — the clip itself WITHOUT its current adjustments, filter and effects, or for an adjustment-layer segment everything on the tracks below it — and analyses it: luminance percentiles set exposure (median towards mid grey without clipping the highlights) and contrast (stretch a flat tonal range), a grey-world estimate on near-neutral midtones sets temperature and tint (removes colour casts such as orange tungsten or blue shade), and low mean chroma raises saturation a little. Writes exposure, contrast, temperature, tint and saturation (other adjustments, HSL and curves are kept; keyframed fields get a keyframe at the playhead). strength scales the correction (0.5 = half). Running it twice gives the same values. Returns the applied values and the measurements. Needs the media to be readable (ffmpeg for video).
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Basic/Auto adjust.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, applied: {exposure, contrast, temperature, tint, saturation}, analysis: {median_luma, black_point, white_point, mean_chroma, cast_rgb}, time_us, keyframed?}.

example1.summary: Fix exposure and white balance of a clip

example2.summary: Gentle correction from the frame at 2 s

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

strength.description: How much of the computed correction to apply, 0..1 (default 1).

time_us.description: Frame to analyse, relative to the segment start. Defaults to the middle of the segment. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Re-frames a clip for another aspect ratio (e.g. landscape 16:9 footage for a 9:16 TikTok/Reels/Shorts canvas) and keeps the main subject in the picture, like CapCut's 'Auto reframe'. The clip is scaled to FILL the target ratio (no bars) and its position is animated with transform.x keyframes (transform.y when the source is taller than the target) that follow the subject: frames are sampled at sample_fps, the subject centre is estimated from motion, edge density and skin-tone cues, and the path is smoothed with a critically damped filter (smoothing 0 = responsive, 1 = very calm camera). Positions are clamped so the clip always covers the canvas. Existing transform.x/y/scale keyframes of the clip are replaced; rotation, crop and animations are kept. With set_canvas=true the project canvas is switched to `ratio` too (other clips are not reframed — run the command for each clip). ratio defaults to the current canvas ratio. Photos get a static best position. Takes about a second per minute of video. One undo step. Undoable.
UI: Toolbar/Auto reframe.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, ratio, canvas_width, canvas_height, canvas_changed, scale, axis: x|y|xy|none, samples, keyframes, track:[{time_us (relative to the clip start), x, y}], note}.

example1.summary: Make a landscape clip vertical and switch the canvas

example2.summary: Square crop that follows the subject calmly

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ratio.description: Target aspect ratio, e.g. 9:16 (vertical), 1:1, 4:5-like 3:4, 16:9. Defaults to the project's canvas ratio.

sample_fps.description: Analysis frames per second of video; higher follows fast motion better but is slower.

segment_id.description: Video or photo clip to reframe.

set_canvas.description: true also changes the project canvas to ratio (what CapCut does); false only reframes the clip.

smoothing.description: Camera smoothness 0..1: 0 follows quick moves, 1 pans slowly (ignores small motion).

zoom.description: Extra zoom on top of the fill scale (1 = just fill, 1.3 = tighter framing).

post.description:
Cancels a queued or running background smart-tool job (e.g. a long background removal). The partial result is discarded and the clips stay as they were; ai.progress reports state 'cancelled'. Cancelling a finished job is a no-op that returns its final state.
Returns: The job {job_id, state, ...} as known when the cancel was requested.

job_id.description: Job to cancel (from ai.remove_background or ai.jobs).

post.description:
Reports which smart tools work on this machine. Scene detection, silence removal, auto reframe and video clean-up only need ffmpeg. Background removal needs a local model provider; the report says which one was found (rembg / onnx / torch), the model file and Python used, which Python packages are importable and where models were searched — or, when none is usable, the error and an install hint (e.g. `pip install rembg onnxruntime`, or put an ONNX matting model at <DataDir>/models/matting.onnx / set KADR_MATTING_MODEL). Detection results are cached; pass refresh=true after installing something. Read-only.
UI: Inspector/Video/Remove BG.
Returns: {ffmpeg, background_removal:{available, provider?, model?, python?, packages?, searched_models?, error?, hint?, checked_at}, commands[]}.

example1.summary: What can the smart tools do here?

refresh.description: true re-runs provider detection instead of using the cached result.

post.description:
Finds the scene changes (camera cuts) inside a video clip without changing anything. ffmpeg's scene detector scores every frame of the clip's source range by how different it is from the previous frame; frames scoring at least `threshold` are cuts. Cut times are mapped onto the timeline with the clip's speed, speed curve and reverse, so time_us can be passed straight to timeline.segment.split. Use it to preview what ai.split_scenes would do, to place markers, or to pick shots. Takes a few seconds per minute of video (results are cached). Read-only.
UI: Toolbar/Split scene.
Returns: {segment_id, threshold, min_scene_us, frames_analyzed, cuts:[{time_us, source_us, score}], scenes:[{start_us, end_us, duration_us}], note}.

example1.summary: Find the cuts in a clip

min_scene_us.description: Shortest scene to keep: cuts closer than this to another (stronger) cut or to the clip edges are ignored (flashes, strobes). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Video clip to analyse (timeline.get lists segment ids).

threshold.description: Scene-change sensitivity: ffmpeg scene score 0..1 a frame must reach. 0.2 = sensitive (also soft cuts), 0.3 = default, 0.5+ = only hard cuts.

post.description:
Lists background smart-tool jobs (currently background removal started by ai.remove_background without wait) with their state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), progress 0..1, frames done and total, estimated seconds left (eta_s, -1 = unknown), the matte file when done, or the error and a hint when failed. The same objects are pushed as 'ai.progress' events. Filter by project_id or fetch one job with job_id. Finished jobs are kept for a while (the last 50). Read-only.
Returns: Array of {job_id, kind, project_id, material_id, segment_ids, provider, model?, state, progress, frames, total_frames, eta_s, matte_path?, error?, hint?, created_at, finished_at?}.

job_id.description: Return only this job (as a one-element list).

project_id.description: Only jobs of this project (omit for all projects).

post.description:
Removes the background of a video, photo or sticker clip automatically (CapCut's 'Remove background → Auto removal'), leaving the person/main subject on a transparent background so lower tracks or the canvas background show through. A local segmentation model computes a greyscale alpha matte per frame (saved in the project cache and recorded as the material's matte_path); the renderer multiplies it into the clip's alpha, so preview, preview.frame and export agree. The matte belongs to the material, so split or duplicated clips of the same file reuse it. Only the frames the project's clips use (+1 s margin) are processed. Providers are detected at run time (see ai.capabilities): Python `rembg`, or `onnxruntime` with an ONNX matting model (KADR_MATTING_MODEL, <DataDir>/models/matting.onnx or rembg's ~/.u2net cache), or `torch` with a TorchScript model; without one the command fails with not_available and an install hint. Matting is slow (roughly 2-10 frames per second on a CPU): by default the command returns at once with state 'running' and a job_id, publishes 'ai.progress' events and, when the matte is ready, applies it as its own undoable step. Agents can pass wait=true to block until it is done (the project cannot be edited meanwhile) and get state 'done'. When a matte already exists the clip is switched on immediately. enabled=false switches the removal off (the matte is kept for later). Undoable.
UI: Inspector/Video/Remove BG.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, state: done|off|running|queued, enabled, job_id?, provider?, model?, matte_path?, reused?, note}. With state running/queued, follow the job with ai.progress events or ai.jobs{job_id}.

example1.summary: Cut out the person in a clip (background job)

enabled.description: true removes the background (computing the matte if needed); false shows the clip unmasked again.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

regenerate.description: true recomputes the matte even when a usable one exists (e.g. after installing a better model).

segment_id.description: Video, photo or sticker clip whose background to remove.

wait.description: true blocks until the matte is computed and returns state done (short clips; matting runs at roughly 2-10 frames/s). If the caller disconnects, the job keeps running and is applied when done. false returns at once with a job_id.

post.description:
Cuts the silent parts out of a clip with sound (talking-head videos, voice-overs, podcasts) and closes the gaps: ffmpeg's silencedetect finds stretches where the clip's own audio stays below threshold_db for at least min_silence_us; padding_us of each silence is kept on both sides so words are not clipped; the remaining parts are joined (ripple). On the main track with the magnet everything after the clip moves left; elsewhere the following clips on the same track move left. Linked clips (e.g. extracted audio) are cut identically. Silence at the clip edges is trimmed too. Works on video clips with an audio stream and on audio clips; times honour speed and reverse. The whole edit is one undo step; removed lists what was cut (timeline times before the ripple). When the entire clip is below the threshold nothing changes and an error explains how to adjust it. Undoable.
UI: Toolbar/Smart tools/Remove silence.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, threshold_db, removed:[{start_us, end_us, duration_us, source_start_us, source_end_us}], removed_total_us, segment_ids[] (remaining clips in order), rippled, note}.

example2.summary: Only long pauses in a noisy room

min_silence_us.description: Shortest pause to remove (timeline time). Shorter pauses are natural speech rhythm and are kept. Unit: microseconds.

padding_us.description: Silence kept on each side of a cut so speech does not start or end abruptly. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Video (with sound) or audio clip to tighten.

threshold_db.description: Audio quieter than this counts as silence. -40 suits clean voice recordings; use -30 for noisy rooms, -50 for very quiet ones. Unit: dBFS.

post.description:
CapCut's 'Split scene': detects the scene changes of a video clip (exactly like ai.detect_scenes) and splits the clip at every cut, so each shot becomes its own clip that can be trimmed, reordered or deleted. Linked clips (e.g. the extracted audio) are split at the same times. The original segment id stays on the first scene; segment_ids lists all resulting clips in timeline order. The whole split is one undo step. When no cut is found nothing changes (lower threshold to be more sensitive). Undoable.
UI: Toolbar/Split scene.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, threshold, min_scene_us, frames_analyzed, cuts[], scenes[], segment_ids[], note}.

example2.summary: Sensitive split, scenes of at least 1 s

min_scene_us.description: Shortest scene to keep: cuts closer than this to another (stronger) cut or to the clip edges are ignored (flashes, strobes). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Video clip to analyse (timeline.get lists segment ids).

threshold.description: Scene-change sensitivity: ffmpeg scene score 0..1 a frame must reach. 0.2 = sensitive (also soft cuts), 0.3 = default, 0.5+ = only hard cuts.

post.description:
Removes the In, Out, Combo or Loop animation of a segment (choosing 'None' in CapCut's Animation tab). kind=all (default) removes every animation. Removing an animation that is not set succeeds without changes.
UI: Inspector/Animation/None.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, animations, loop_animation?} after removal.

kind.description: Which animation to remove; all removes in, out, combo and loop.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Applies an In, Out or Combo animation preset to a video, photo, sticker or text segment — the Animation tab in CapCut (In plays at the start, Out at the end, Combo runs across the clip). id comes from library.list {kind: "animation"} and is kind-qualified ("in_fade", "out_zoom_out", "combo_swing", "loop_pulse"); an id whose prefix names another slot is rejected. Setting a Combo removes In and Out, and setting In or Out removes Combo, like CapCut. duration_us defaults to 0.5 s for in/out and to the whole segment for combo, and is clamped to the segment; when in+out would exceed the segment, the other one is shortened. kind=loop adds a repeating animation (duration = one cycle, default 1 s) that runs for the whole clip on any picture segment (video, photo, sticker, text) and combines with In/Out/Combo.
UI: Inspector/Animation.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, animations: {in?, out?, combo?}, loop_animation?}.

duration_us.description: Animation length; default 500000 for in/out, the segment length for combo, 1000000 for loop. Unit: microseconds.

id.description: Animation id from library.list {kind: "animation"}, e.g. "in_fade", "out_slide_left" or "combo_swing".

kind.description: Animation slot: in (start), out (end), combo (whole clip) or loop (repeats for the whole clip).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Tells where this Kadr serves its local REST/WebSocket API (the same API kadrctl, kadr-mcp and AI agents use) — Settings → API. Returns the configured host and port, where they come from (source: env = the KADR_ADDR environment variable, settings = settings.json "api" saved by app.api.set, default = 127.0.0.1:7777), the URL clients should use right now, the token file that holds the Bearer token this API accepts, and the endpoint file (<data folder>/api-endpoint.json) that every running Kadr writes so tools find it automatically. listening=false or fallback=true means the configured port was busy: error and hint explain what holds it (another program, or another Kadr) and how to fix it. Read-only; never returns the token itself.
UI: Settings/API.
Returns: {host, port, url, docs, source env|settings|default, allow_remote, settings{host, port, allow_remote}, env_override?, token_file, endpoint_file, listening, listen_addr, fallback?, mode editor|headless, pid, error?, hint?, warning?}.

Changes the port (and optionally the host) of the local API and saves it in settings.json "api" — Settings → API → Port. The editor window moves the API immediately, without a restart: it binds the new port first (if that fails nothing changes and the error says why), then stops the old listener after this response is sent, rewrites <data folder>/api-endpoint.json and publishes app.api.changed. A headless kadr-server also moves live. kadrctl and kadr-mcp follow automatically because they read api-endpoint.json; scripts with a hard-coded address must use the returned url. The token does not change. Ports below 1024 are refused. host 127.0.0.1 (default) or localhost keep the API private to this computer; 0.0.0.0 exposes it to the network (token still required) and needs allow_remote=true. When KADR_ADDR is set it overrides the setting for this process: the value is saved but takes effect only when KADR_ADDR is removed (see warning). Calling it with the current values changes nothing. App setting, not a project edit: not undoable.
UI: Settings/API.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: Same as app.api.get plus changed (always present; false when nothing changed) and previous_url (set when it changed); warning explains a KADR_ADDR override or the risk of host 0.0.0.0.

allow_remote.description: Confirms exposing the API to other computers when host is 0.0.0.0. Anyone on the network who has the token can then control Kadr.

host.description: Listen host: "127.0.0.1" (default, this computer only), "localhost", or "0.0.0.0" (all network interfaces; requires allow_remote=true). Omit to keep it.

port.description: TCP port for the API, 1024..65535 (default 7777). Omit to keep the current port. Unit: port.

post.description:
Returns information about this Kadr installation — what the About section of Settings shows: the version (semver, e.g. 1.0.0; prerelease=true only for builds such as 1.1.0-beta.1), build details (git revision and time when available), Go version, OS and CPU architecture, the executable path, the data folder (projects, settings.json, api-token), whether it is a portable build, whether FFmpeg was found (path, version and where it came from), the active renderer with the current render settings (GPU adapter and backend, or the CPU fallback and why) and the GitHub repository used for updates (private: Kadr is distributed by invitation, see update.check). Use it to report bugs or to decide whether update.check / tools.install_ffmpeg are needed. Read-only and offline.
UI: Settings/About.
Returns: {name, version, prerelease, go_version, os, arch, build{module, vcs.revision?, vcs.time?, vcs.modified?}, executable, data_dir, portable, ffmpeg{found, ffmpeg_path, ffprobe_path, version, source, error}, update_repo, update_channel, update_signing_key, website, releases_url (private repository), changelog_url (public release notes), renderer{kind gpu|cpu, backend?, device?, vendor?, vram_total_mb?, vram_cap_mb?, vram_used_mb, reason? (why the CPU renders)} — the same shape as export.status renderer}.

Takes back "Always for this chat" (assistant.approve decision always): the named command, or every command when command is omitted, no longer runs without asking in this chat — the chat's permission mode decides again (ask_every asks before every change, ask_risky before risky ones). The current list is always_allow of assistant.session. Works while the chat is running (the next call is checked against the new list). A status event with state always_allow (message and the remaining commands) is stored in the transcript and published as assistant.status. Fails with not_found when the named command is not always allowed; clearing an empty list does nothing.
Returns: {removed: [commands that ask again], always_allow: [commands still always allowed]}.

command.description: Command to ask about again (e.g. "project.delete"); omit to clear the whole list.

project_id.description: Project the chat belongs to ("prj_…"). Omit for chats without a project; for an existing session it only narrows the search.

session_id.description: Chat session id ("ses_…") from assistant.sessions, assistant.new or assistant.send.

post.summary: Stop always allowing in AI chat
post.x-user-only: The built-in AI assistant's settings, chats, sign-ins and keys belong to the user (the AI panel in Kadr's title bar); other AI agents do not see or drive it.

post.description:
Answers an approval card of a running chat (assistant.approval_request event): allow runs the action, deny tells the assistant the user refused (it will not retry), always allows it and every later call of the same command in this chat without asking (not offered for paid generation, which is confirmed every time; assistant.always_allow.revoke takes it back). The permission_resolved event says always=true then. For paid generation the approved call gets the estimate's confirm token automatically. Unanswered cards are denied after 10 minutes.
Returns: {ok: true}.

decision.description: allow, deny, or always (allow this command for the rest of the chat).

message.description: Optional note for the assistant when denying (e.g. "use the local voice instead").

request_id.description: Id of the approval card (permission.id of the event, "perm_…").

session_id.description: Chat session id ("ses_…") from assistant.sessions, assistant.new or assistant.send.

post.x-user-only: The built-in AI assistant's settings, chats, sign-ins and keys belong to the user (the AI panel in Kadr's title bar); other AI agents do not see or drive it.

post.description:
Stops an install or sign-in started with assistant.cli.install / assistant.cli.login (by job_id or agent id): the installer or login process is ended and assistant.cli.done reports canceled. Returns canceled=false when nothing was running.
Returns: {canceled: bool}.

job_id.description: Job id returned by install/login (or the agent id).

post.x-user-only: The built-in AI assistant's settings, chats, sign-ins and keys belong to the user (the AI panel in Kadr's title bar); other AI agents do not see or drive it.

post.description:
Adds, replaces or removes a user-defined CLI agent. spec describes how to run it: command, args (templates with {prompt}, {mcp_config}, {mcp_config_json}, {mcp_url}, {kadr_mcp}, {session}, {model}, {workdir}, {instructions}), resume_args, model_args, prompt_via (arg|stdin), output (stream-json for Claude-compatible JSON, jsonl, plain), transport (stdio|gateway), tools (meta = five meta-tools, the default | full = one tool per command), env (KEY=value), key_env (names filled from the vault), session_pattern. Custom agents are not limited to Kadr's tools, so chats using them need allow_outside. Saved in the assistant settings.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {id, removed?} or the agent's status entry.

example1.summary: Add an agent that prints plain text

id.description: Agent id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (e.g. my-agent).

spec.description: The CustomSpec (see description); required unless remove=true.

post.x-user-only: The built-in AI assistant's settings, chats, sign-ins and keys belong to the user (the AI panel in Kadr's title bar); other AI agents do not see or drive it.

post.description:
Installs a coding-agent CLI with its official install command (npm -g, winget, Homebrew, pip or the vendor's script — see install methods in assistant.cli.status). Runs in the background and returns a job_id; the installer's output streams as assistant.cli.output events {job_id, agent, job, line, stream} and the end as assistant.cli.done {job_id, agent, job, ok, error?, status}. wait=true blocks instead. assistant.cli.cancel stops it. Needs the tool the method requires (npm for most agents: install Node.js first).
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {started: true, job_id, agent, job: "install"} (background) or {job_id, ok, status} with wait=true.

agent.description: CLI agent id: claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, cursor, copilot, opencode, qwen, amp, goose, crush, kimi, aider, cline, droid, warp, or a custom id ("cli:" prefix allowed).

method.description: Install method id from the agent's install list (npm, winget, brew, script…); default: the first one available on this OS.

wait.description: Block until the installer finishes and return the new status.

post.x-user-only: The built-in AI assistant's settings, chats, sign-ins and keys belong to the user (the AI panel in Kadr's title bar); other AI agents do not see or drive it.

post.description:
Signs a CLI agent in ("Sign in" in the settings). Without api_key it runs the CLI's own sign-in: the provider's page opens in the browser (or a terminal window for CLIs that only sign in interactively) and Kadr polls until the agent reports it is signed in, the login ends or 5 minutes pass — in the background with a job_id, output lines (URLs, device codes) as assistant.cli.output and the end as assistant.cli.done {job_id, agent, ok, status}. With api_key the key is stored in the OS-encrypted vault for the agent's auth variable (env, default the agent's first auth key) and the new status is returned at once.
Risk: secret — handles credentials; only the user runs it (agents never send, read or change keys and passwords).
Returns: {started: true, job_id, agent, job: "login"} (background), {job_id, ok, status} with wait=true, or {ok, status} with api_key.

example2.summary: Use an API key for Gemini CLI

agent.description: CLI agent id: claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, cursor, copilot, opencode, qwen, amp, goose, crush, kimi, aider, cline, droid, warp, or a custom id ("cli:" prefix allowed).

api_key.description: Sign in with this API key / token instead of the browser login (stored in the vault).

env.description: Environment variable for api_key (one of the agent's key_specs; default its first auth key).

terminal.description: Open a visible terminal window even when the CLI has a non-interactive login.

wait.description: Block until the sign-in finishes and return the status.

post.x-user-only: API keys and passwords are managed only by the user in Kadr's Settings; AI agents never see, add, test or change them.

post.description:
Stores an API key or token for a CLI agent (one of its key_specs, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for Claude Code, OPENAI_API_KEY for Codex, GEMINI_API_KEY for Gemini CLI) in Kadr's OS-encrypted vault; it reaches the CLI only through its environment when Kadr starts it and is never shown again (status lists only the names of stored keys). An empty value removes the stored key. Plain settings of a spec (secret=false, e.g. a base URL) are stored the same way.
Risk: secret — handles credentials; only the user runs it (agents never send, read or change keys and passwords).
Returns: {agent, env, stored: bool}.

agent.description: CLI agent id: claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, cursor, copilot, opencode, qwen, amp, goose, crush, kimi, aider, cline, droid, warp, or a custom id ("cli:" prefix allowed).

env.description: Environment variable name from the agent's key_specs (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

value.description: The key / token (single line); "" removes it.

post.x-user-only: API keys and passwords are managed only by the user in Kadr's Settings; AI agents never see, add, test or change them.

post.description:

post.description:
Finds the beats/onsets (drum hits, note attacks) of an audio clip or of a video clip's sound, like CapCut's auto Beat feature, and returns their times on the TIMELINE in microseconds (speed and reverse of the segment are taken into account; only beats inside the segment's timeline range are returned). The source range is decoded to mono 11025 Hz and analysed in pure Go: spectral flux of the log-magnitude spectrum (512-sample window, 11.6 ms hop), adaptive threshold (local mean + delta) with peak picking, then each beat is refined in the time domain to the attack sample (typically within a few milliseconds). bpm is a rough tempo from the median beat interval. With add_markers=true a timeline marker labelled "Beat" is added at every beat (existing markers within 10 ms are kept, not duplicated) so clips can be snapped to the music. At most the first 20 minutes of the clip are analysed. Without add_markers the project is unchanged (note: the call is still recorded as an undo step).
UI: Toolbar/Beat.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, beats_us[] (timeline µs, ascending), strengths[] (0..1 per beat), count, bpm (0 when fewer than 4 beats), sensitivity, markers_added, analyzed_us}.

CapCut's "Extract audio": separates the sound of a video clip into its own audio clip. A new segment with the same material, source range, timeline range, speed (incl. keep_pitch/curve), reverse flag, volume, fades, volume keyframes, voice effect, noise reduction and loudness normalisation is placed on the first unlocked audio track that is free at that time range (a new audio track is created otherwise). The video segment is muted (volume 0, its volume keyframes move to the audio clip) and both segments are linked with a shared link_group so they move/trim together while timeline linkage is on (an existing link_group of the video segment is reused). Works on video clips on the main or overlay tracks whose material has an audio stream; fails with invalid_argument for photos, freeze frames or silent videos, and with conflict when the clip's track is locked or its audio was already extracted.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Extract audio.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {video_segment_id, audio_segment_id, audio_track_id, created_track, link_group}.

example1.summary: Separate the sound of a clip

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Measures the loudness of a clip's sound over its source range with ffmpeg's ebur128 filter (EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770-4: K-weighted, gated integrated loudness in LUFS, loudness range in LU and true peak in dBFS; mono sources are measured as dual-mono because they play on both channels). Speed, reverse and voice effects are not applied to the measurement. Also reports the clip volume in dB, the gain that "Normalize loudness" applies (brings the clip to target_lufs = -14 LUFS, but never lifts the true peak above -1 dBTP; limited to -30..+20 dB) and effective_lufs = integrated + volume_db (+ normalize gain when enabled). Silence reports -70 LUFS / -144 dBFS. Useful for AI agents balancing music against voice-over: e.g. keep background music ~10-15 LU below speech. Results are cached per file and range.
UI: Inspector/Audio/Basic.
Returns: {segment_id, integrated_lufs, loudness_range_lu, true_peak_dbfs, volume_db, normalize_gain_db, normalize_enabled, effective_lufs, target_lufs, source_start_us, source_duration_us, method}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Undoes a separation at any later time (CapCut's "Restore audio"): deletes the audio clip that audio.separate / audio.extract created from a video clip and gives the video its sound back. Pass EITHER segment of the pair: the video clip (main/overlay track) or the separated audio clip (same material and link_group on an audio track). The video gets the audio clip's current volume, fades, volume keyframes, voice effect, noise reduction and loudness normalisation, so it sounds as before; trims or moves made to the audio clip alone are dropped (the video plays its own source range). If the separated audio was split, every piece is removed. An audio track left empty is deleted, and the link_group is cleared when no other clip remains linked. Fails with invalid_argument when the clip has no separated audio, and with conflict when one of the tracks is locked.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Restore audio.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {video_segment_id, removed_segment_ids[], removed_track_ids[], volume_db (restored video volume, -144 = muted), link_group}.

example1.summary: Put the sound back into a video clip

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
CapCut's "Separate audio" (Ctrl+Shift+S): moves the sound of a video clip into its own audio clip on an audio track, exactly like audio.extract. The new audio segment copies the material, source and timeline range, speed (incl. keep_pitch/curve), reverse, volume, fades, volume keyframes, voice effect, noise reduction and loudness normalisation; it goes on the first unlocked audio track that is free at that time (a new audio track otherwise). The video clip is muted (volume 0) and both clips share a link_group, so they move/trim/delete together while timeline linkage is on. Undo it with edit.undo, or later with audio.restore (puts the sound back into the video). Fails with invalid_argument for photos, freeze frames, non-video clips and videos without an audio stream, and with conflict when the track is locked or the sound was already separated.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Separate audio. Hotkey: Ctrl+Shift+S.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {video_segment_id, audio_segment_id, audio_track_id, created_track, link_group}.

example1.summary: Separate the sound of the selected clip

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Lists the built-in voice changer presets (Audio inspector → Voice changer): id, display name, category (Character, Space, Device, Fun, Studio) and what each sounds like (25 presets: pitch, reverbs, radios, ring modulation, whisper, studio enhancement...). Apply one with segment.set_audio{segment_id, voice_effect: <id>}; an empty voice_effect removes it. Effects are rendered with ffmpeg filters during preview and export and keep the clip's timing (pitch effects use pitch-shift + tempo correction).
UI: Inspector/Audio/Voice changer.
Returns: Array of {id, name, category, description}.

Adds a caption cue typed by hand (CapCut's Manual captions) on the caption track at at_us (default: the playhead). It takes the look and position of the existing captions on that track (or style_id, or the default style) and gets estimated word timings so highlight styles work. When the next cue starts earlier than at_us + duration_us the new cue is shortened to fit; starting inside an existing cue is a conflict.
UI: Library/Captions/Manual captions.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, track_id, cue: {segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id, words}}.

at_us.description: Start on the timeline (default: the playhead). Unit: microseconds.

duration_us.description: Length of the cue (default 2 s). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

style_id.description: Caption style id from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. cap_clean, cap_highlight_word, cap_karaoke_bar, cap_pop_word, cap_box_dark.

track_id.description: Text track (default: the first caption track, created when missing).

post.description:
Reports whether local speech recognition (auto captions, transcripts) works on this computer: the Python interpreter found (KADR_PYTHON overrides it), the faster-whisper version, whether an NVIDIA GPU is usable, which Whisper models are downloaded (tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3 — Kadr never downloads models itself), plus the list of recognisable languages and the defaults. When unavailable, code/message/hint explain what to install. The first call takes a few seconds (it starts Python); the answer is cached.
Returns: {available, engine, python, python_version, version, cuda, models: {tiny: true, …}, code?, message?, hint?, default_model, models_list, devices, languages: [{code, name}]}.

refresh.description: Probe again instead of using the cached answer (after installing something).

post.description:
Generates captions from the speech in the timeline, like CapCut's Captions → Auto captions → Generate, but fully offline: the sound of every audible clip (main track, overlays and audio tracks; muted tracks and clips with volume 0 are skipped — or only segment_ids) is recognised locally with Whisper (faster-whisper in a Python subprocess, word-level timestamps), the words are stored on each material as its transcript (source time, reused next time — see transcript.get) and turned into caption cues on a text track named "Captions": at most max_lines lines of max_chars characters, split at sentences, commas and pauses, each cue carrying per-word timings (TextStyle.words, relative to the cue start) so word-highlight caption styles animate. Existing cues on the Captions track over the transcribed clips are replaced (replace=false adds a second track). Recognition runs as a background job: the call returns {job_id, state…} at once; follow captions.progress events or poll captions.status {job_id} (or pass wait=true to block until done — fine for clips of a few minutes). Creating the cues is ONE undo step ("Create captions from transcript"); transcripts themselves are analysis data and are not undone. Errors not_available (code "not_available") when Python/faster-whisper/the model is missing — see captions.asr_status. Typical speed: small model ≈ 5× real time on an NVIDIA GPU, ≈ 1× on a CPU.
UI: Library/Captions/Auto captions.
Returns: Job status {job_id, project_id, kind: "captions", state: queued|running|done|failed|cancelled, phase, progress 0..1, material_ids (being transcribed), language, detected_languages, model, device, media_s, elapsed_s, error?, result?}. When done, result = captions.from_transcript's result {track_id, count, segment_ids, words, languages, removed, transcribed: [{material_id, language, words, text}]}.

example2.summary: Ukrainian speech, wait for the result

example3.summary: One clip, word-highlight style, fast model

device.description: Where recognition runs: auto (CUDA GPU when usable, else CPU int8), cuda or cpu. A failing GPU falls back to the CPU.

force.description: Transcribe again even when the material already has a transcript (e.g. to use a bigger model).

language.description: Spoken language: "auto" (detect, default) or a code/name such as en, uk, es, de, fr, pt, ru, zh, ja, ko, ar, hi, it, nl, pl, tr, vi, th, id, ms, bn, my, ro, tl (Filipino). Locales ("en-US") and English names ("Ukrainian") are accepted. captions.asr_status lists all ~100 languages.

max_chars.description: Characters per line (default from the style, 42 for cap_clean; reduced automatically on portrait canvases).

max_lines.description: Lines per caption (default 2, from the style).

max_words.description: Words per caption; 0 = no limit, 1 = one word at a time (default from the style).

model.description: Whisper model size: tiny (fastest, least accurate), base, small (default: good accuracy, ~1× real time on a CPU, ~5× faster on an NVIDIA GPU), medium, large-v3 (best, slow without a GPU). Only models already downloaded can be used.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

prompt.description: Optional hint text for the recogniser: names, jargon or spelling to prefer (e.g. "Kadr, CapCut, Kyiv").

replace.description: Replace existing cues on the Captions track over the captioned clips (default). false keeps them and puts the new captions on a new track.

segment_id.description: Shortcut for a single clip (same as segment_ids with one id).

segment_ids.description: Only caption these clips (ids of video/audio clips with sound). Omit to caption every audible clip.

style_id.description: Caption style from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. "cap_highlight_word" (default: the style of the existing captions, else "cap_clean").

wait.description: true = block until the job finishes and return its final status (with the result); false (default) = return the job right away and report progress through captions.progress events / captions.status.

post.description:
Stops a running or queued captions.auto / transcript.transcribe job: the recognition process is killed, nothing is written to the project (transcripts already saved for other materials stay). Cancelling a finished job does nothing and returns its final status.
Returns: The job status (state "cancelled" unless it had already finished).

job_id.description: Job id returned by captions.auto or transcript.transcribe.

post.description:
Deletes caption cues (no ripple: the video is not changed — use transcript.delete_words to cut speech). Pass segment_id / segment_ids, or all=true to clear every caption track (or only track_id). Caption tracks left empty are removed.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {deleted: [segment ids], count}.

all.description: Delete every cue of every caption track (or of track_id).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Cue to delete.

track_id.description: With all=true: only this text track.

post.description:
Exports the captions (CapCut's Download captions): SubRip (srt), WebVTT (vtt), plain text (txt — one cue per line, a transcript) or LRC lyrics (lrc). By default the cues of every caption track are exported in timeline order; when the project has no caption track, every text segment is. Pass track_id for one text track. With path the file is written (folders are created, existing files overwritten); without path the text is returned in content. The project is not modified.
UI: Library/Captions/Download captions.
Returns: {format, count, path? (when written), content? (when path is omitted)}.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to write, e.g. C:\Users\me\Videos\captions.srt. Omit to get the text back.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: Only export this text track.

post.description:
Writes the project's text segments to a SubRip (.srt) file — Captions → Export. By default every text segment of every text track is exported in timeline order (overlapping texts from different tracks become separate cues); pass track_id to export a single caption track. The project is not modified. Existing files are overwritten; the folder must exist.
UI: Library/Captions/Export.
Returns: {path, count}.

path.description: Absolute path of the .srt file to write, e.g. C:\Users\me\Videos\captions.srt.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: Only export this text track.

post.description:
Creates caption cues from the transcripts already stored on the materials (made by captions.auto or transcript.transcribe) without running speech recognition again — e.g. after editing the video, or to re-caption with other line rules. Words heard in the chosen clips (or every audible clip) are mapped to timeline time (speed, speed curves and reverse are honoured) and grouped into cues: a new cue starts after a pause of 0.7 s, after a sentence, or when max_lines × max_chars would overflow (preferring a comma in the second half); lines are balanced. Each cue is a text segment on the "Captions" track with text.words = per-word timings relative to the cue start (for word-highlight styles). With replace=true (default) existing cues on the caption track over those clips are removed first, and when style_id is omitted the look and position of the existing captions are kept. One undo step.
UI: Library/Captions/Create from transcript.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, count, segment_ids (new cues), words, languages, style_id, removed (old cues removed), untranscribed_segment_ids}.

max_chars.description: Characters per line (default from the style; 42 for cap_clean, fewer on portrait canvases).

max_lines.description: Lines per cue (default from the style, usually 2).

max_words.description: Words per cue; 0 = no limit, 1 = one word at a time (default from the style).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

replace.description: Remove existing cues that overlap the captioned clips (default true). false = a new caption track.

segment_ids.description: Clips to caption (default: every audible clip whose material has a transcript).

style_id.description: Caption style id from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. cap_clean, cap_highlight_word, cap_karaoke_bar, cap_pop_word, cap_box_dark.

track_id.description: Text track to fill (default: the existing Captions track, or a new one).

post.description:
Imports a subtitle file as caption cues (CapCut's Upload caption file): SubRip .srt, WebVTT .vtt, Advanced SubStation .ass/.ssa (Dialogue lines; override tags stripped, \N = line break) or LRC lyrics .lrc ([mm:ss.xx] lines, [offset:], enhanced <mm:ss.xx> word tags become word timings). The format comes from the extension (or format). Cues go to a new "Captions" text track (or track_id / the existing caption track with replace=true) in the chosen caption style, shifted by offset_us; overlapping cues are trimmed. Without word timings in the file they are estimated from the text so word-highlight styles work. One undo step.
UI: Library/Captions/Upload caption file.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, count, segment_ids, skipped (cues before 0), format}.

estimate_words.description: Give cues without word timings estimated ones (proportional to word length).

format.description: srt, vtt, ass or lrc (default: from the file extension / content).

offset_us.description: Shift every cue by this much (negative = earlier; cues ending before 0 are dropped). Unit: microseconds.

path.description: Absolute path of the subtitle file (UTF-8).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

replace.description: Clear the target caption track (track_id or the existing Captions track) first.

track_id.description: Text track to fill; it must be free where the cues go unless replace=true.

post.description:
Imports a SubRip (.srt) subtitle file as text segments — one per cue — on a new text track (or on track_id), like Captions → Import captions. Timings come from the file (shifted by offset_us); overlapping cues are trimmed so they do not overlap, formatting tags such as <i> are stripped and multi-line cues keep their line breaks. Captions use the "Caption" look (white, size 9, thin black outline) or template_id, and sit in the lower part of the frame (transform y = 0.6, i.e. centred at 80% of the height). Edit any caption afterwards with text.update.
UI: Library/Captions/Import captions.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, count, segment_ids: [...], skipped: cues dropped because they ended before 0}.

offset_us.description: Shift every cue by this much on the timeline (may be negative; cues before 0 are dropped). Unit: microseconds.

path.description: Absolute path of the .srt file to import (UTF-8).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

template_id.description: Text template for the captions, e.g. "caption_box" or "caption_yellow" (default "caption_classic").

track_id.description: Existing text track to fill; it must be free where the captions go. Omit to create a new text track.

post.description:
Lists the caption cues — the caption editor's list: every text segment on caption tracks (text tracks named "Captions…", created by captions.auto / captions.import / captions.import_srt) in timeline order, with text, start/end, the caption style and the word timings (relative to the cue start). Pass track_id to list any text track. Use the segment ids with captions.update / split / merge / delete / set_style.
UI: Library/Captions.
Returns: {tracks: [{track_id, name, count, locked}], count, cues: [{segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id?, words?: [{text, start_us, end_us}]}]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: List this text track only (default: all caption tracks).

post.description:
Joins caption cues into one — Delete at the start of a cue in the caption editor merges it with the previous one. Pass segment_id with direction (next = merge with the following cue, previous = with the preceding one) or segment_ids (two or more cues of the same track). The result spans from the first start to the last end, keeps the first cue's look, joins the texts (re-wrapped into balanced lines) and keeps every word timing.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The merged cue {segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id, words}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Cue to merge with its neighbour (see direction).

segment_ids.description: Alternatively: the cues to merge (same track; everything between them is merged too).

post.description:
Re-splits caption cues from their word timings with new line rules — characters per line, lines per cue and words per cue (e.g. max_words=3 for punchy short captions, max_chars=32 for narrow vertical video). Cues are regrouped at pauses and sentence ends exactly like auto captions; their look and position are kept. Cues without word timings are left alone. Omitted rules come from each track's caption style.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {count: cues after the change, segment_ids}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: Only this text track (default: every caption track).

post.description:
Applies a caption style (library.list kind=caption_style) to every cue of every caption track, or to track_id / segment_ids — like picking a style in CapCut's caption panel. The look (font, size, colours, outline, shadow, box, glow, gradient, letter case and the active-word highlight: color, box/pill, scale, underline, karaoke, pop, bounce, reveal, dim, glow, sweep_line or slide_box) is replaced; text and word timings are kept; cues move to the style's vertical position unless keep_position=true. Styles that show a fixed number of words at a time (cap_pop_word = 1, cap_sunset_gradient = 3) re-split the cues from their word timings (relayout); switching back to a normal style re-joins them. The highlight is drawn by the text renderer from text.words + text.highlight.
UI: Library/Captions/Styles.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {style_id, count (cues styled), relayout: bool, segment_ids (cue ids after the change)}.

keep_position.description: Keep each cue's current position instead of the style's.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

relayout.description: Force (true) or prevent (false) re-splitting the cues with the style's line rules. Default: only when the words-per-cue rule changes.

style_id.description: Caption style id from library.list kind=caption_style, e.g. cap_clean, cap_highlight_word, cap_karaoke_bar, cap_pop_word, cap_box_dark.

track_id.description: Only the cues of this text track.

post.description:
Moves caption cues in time by offset_us (negative = earlier) to fix out-of-sync subtitles: every cue of every caption track by default, or only segment_ids, or the cues of track_id, optionally only those starting at or after from_us. Word timings move with their cues. Cues may not start before 0 or overlap cues that stay in place (conflict).
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {shifted: count, offset_us}.

from_us.description: Only cues starting at or after this time. Unit: microseconds.

offset_us.description: How far to move (e.g. 500000 = half a second later, -250000 = a quarter second earlier). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: Only the cues of this text track.

post.description:
Splits a caption cue in two — what pressing Enter in the caption editor does. Give the split point as at_char (a character offset in the text, as a JavaScript caret position), at_word (index of the first word of the second cue) or at_us (timeline time; default: the playhead). With word timings the time split happens where the first word of the second part starts; without, in proportion to the text length. Both parts keep the look and position.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {left: cue, right: cue}.

at_char.description: Split the text at this character offset (UTF-16 units, like a textarea's selectionStart).

at_us.description: Split at this timeline time (default: the playhead when neither at_char nor at_word is given). Unit: microseconds.

at_word.description: Index of the first word of the second cue (0-based word index into the cue's words).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the caption cue (a text segment), e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from captions.list.

post.description:
Returns the status of a captions.auto / transcript.transcribe job: state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), phase (waiting, extracting_audio, loading_model, transcribing, creating_captions, finished), progress 0..1, the device used and, when done, the result. With wait_s the call blocks until the job finishes or the time runs out (long polling — convenient for AI agents). Without job_id it lists the recent jobs of project_id (or of all projects), newest first. Jobs live in memory and are forgotten when Kadr restarts.
Returns: With job_id: the job status (see captions.auto). Without: {jobs: [job status…]}.

job_id.description: Job id returned by captions.auto or transcript.transcribe, e.g. "cap_1a2b3c4d5e6f".

project_id.description: Without job_id: only list the jobs of this project.

wait_s.description: With job_id: wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish before answering (0 = answer now). Unit: seconds.

post.description:
Edits one caption cue: its text (inline editing in the caption list; \n breaks lines) and/or its start and end on the timeline (time nudge). When the text changes, words that are still there keep their recognised timings and new/changed words share the time between them, so word highlighting stays in sync. Times may not overlap the neighbouring cues on the track (conflict). At least one of text, start_us, end_us is needed.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated cue {segment_id, track_id, index, start_us, end_us, text, style_id, words}.

end_us.description: New end on the timeline (exclusive). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the caption cue (a text segment), e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from captions.list.

start_us.description: New start on the timeline. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Copies clips to the editor's clipboard (kept in memory per project, not the OS clipboard) so they can be pasted with clipboard.paste — Ctrl+C in CapCut. All properties are copied (effects, filters, keyframes, text style…). Linked clips are copied along when linkage is on. The project is not changed and nothing is added to undo history.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Copy. Hotkey: Ctrl+C.
Returns: {copied: [segment ids]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the clip. Required unless segment_ids is given.

segment_ids.description: Several segment ids at once (multi-selection). Combined with segment_id when both are given.

post.description:
Copies clips to the editor's clipboard and deletes them from the timeline — Ctrl+X in CapCut. Deletion follows timeline.segment.delete (ripple on the magnet main track, linked clips included, emptied tracks removed). Undo restores the clips; the clipboard keeps the copy.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Cut. Hotkey: Ctrl+X.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {cut: [segment ids]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the clip. Required unless segment_ids is given.

segment_ids.description: Several segment ids at once (multi-selection). Combined with segment_id when both are given.

post.description:
Pastes the clips from clipboard.copy / clipboard.cut at at_us (default: the playhead) — Ctrl+V in CapCut. Clips keep their timing relative to each other and get new ids (pasted linked clips are linked to each other). Each clip goes back to its original track if it still exists (or to track_id when given and compatible); on the main track the magnet inserts at the nearest clip boundary and ripples, and the rest of the pasted selection follows by the same amount; on other tracks an occupied spot sends the clip to a new track. Transitions are not pasted. Fails with conflict when the clipboard is empty.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Paste. Hotkey: Ctrl+V.

post.description:
Cancels a queued or running export — the Cancel button of the export progress view. A running job's FFmpeg process is killed and the partially written file is deleted; the call waits (up to 10 s) until the job has stopped and returns its final state "cancelled" (an export.cancelled event is published). Cancelling an already cancelled job is a no-op; cancelling a done or failed job returns conflict (delete the file yourself if needed).
UI: Export dialog/Cancel.
Returns: The job object (same shape as export.status), normally with state "cancelled".

post.description:

The size is bitrate × duration for video/audio (real files are usually a bit smaller with simple content) and a heuristic for GIF. encoder is the FFmpeg encoder that will be used (e.g. h264_nvenc, hevc_amf, h264_qsv, h264_videotoolbox or libx264; the encoder of the GPU Kadr renders on is preferred); it is empty until hardware detection has finished (it starts on the first call).

post.description:
Starts exporting the project to a file in the background and returns immediately with a job_id — the Export button in the top bar. The project is snapshotted at this moment, so later edits do not change a running export. Every frame is rendered by the same compositor as the player and encoded with FFmpeg (H.264 or HEVC in MP4/MOV, 4:2:0 8-bit, BT.709 limited range, AAC 192 kbps stereo audio, +faststart for instant web playback). GPU rendering: when a GPU can be used (render.settings.get; NVIDIA, AMD, Intel via Vulkan/D3D12, Apple via Metal) every frame is composited on the GPU and handed to the encoder as NV12 without any CPU conversion; the hardware encoder of the same GPU (NVENC, AMF, Quick Sync, VideoToolbox) is used when it works (on an RTX 3060 a 1080p H.264 export of a real project runs at about 250 frames per second, roughly 6x the CPU renderer). The render.* settings apply: render.settings.set mode=cpu forces the CPU renderer, mode=gpu fails the export instead of falling back, and vram_limit_mb/reserve_mb cap the video memory Kadr uses (frames in flight, caches, the hardware decoders and the hardware encoder are sized from the cap; under 1024 MB the export decodes and encodes in software and says so in its warnings). If the GPU fails during the export (driver reset, device lost, out of video memory) the remaining frames are rendered on the CPU and the job finishes with a warning (export.status warnings; renderer.kind becomes "cpu"). Exports longer than 4 minutes are encoded in 2-minute parts joined at the end without re-encoding; an encoder that fails or stops responding (driver hiccup) is checked again and the export goes on from the part that failed, switching to the software encoder only when the hardware encoder fails its check (also with a warning; it is checked again before the next export). The soundtrack is mixed while the frames render. Set audio_only=true for an MP3/WAV/AAC/FLAC soundtrack, or gif=true for an animated GIF. Use range_start_us/range_end_us to export part of the timeline. Jobs run one at a time by default (others wait in state "queued"; KADR_EXPORT_CONCURRENCY raises it). Follow progress with export.status (poll every 1-2 s) or the export.progress / export.done / export.failed / export.cancelled / export.warning events; stop with export.cancel. Call export.estimate first to preview size and path. Does not modify the project and is not undoable. It is a global command (project_id is passed explicitly) so it cannot be part of a batch or dry run. Fails with invalid_argument when the timeline is empty.
UI: Top bar/Export. Hotkey: Ctrl+E.
Returns: {job_id, state ("queued"|"running"), path (final file path, already made unique), kind (video|audio|gif), width, height, fps, frames, duration_us, bitrate_kbps, codec, format, estimated_size_bytes}.

Returns the current state of one export job: state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), phase (starting, video, encoding, finalizing; audio only for audio-only exports), progress 0..1, frames_done/frames_total, speed_fps (frames encoded per second over the last few seconds), eta_s (seconds left from the frames left and that speed, -1 while unknown), elapsed_s, audio_progress (0..1, the soundtrack is mixed while the frames render), output path, size_bytes once done, the encoder used (e.g. h264_nvenc, hevc_amf, h264_videotoolbox or libx264), renderer {kind "gpu"|"cpu", backend (vulkan, d3d12, metal), device (adapter name), vendor, vram_total_mb, vram_cap_mb (the cap from render.settings), vram_used_mb (textures and buffers Kadr allocated), vram_process_mb (video memory the OS charges to Kadr's process now, kept under the cap), reason (why the CPU renders)}, warnings (problems the job recovered from: the GPU failed mid-export and the CPU finished it, an encoder failed or stopped responding and the export went on from the part that failed, the hardware encoder failed its check and the software encoder restarted the job, effects without a GPU version) and the error message on failure. post.description:
Lists Kadr's curated catalogue of downloadable font families — the "More fonts" section of the Text → Font picker. Every family is free and open-source (SIL Open Font License 1.1) from the google/fonts repository; most support Cyrillic (cyrillic=true; ukrainian is verified after installation). Each entry has an id (also the font id to use in text.update font once installed), name, style category (sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace, pixel), a short note on its look and best use, download size, the exact file URLs, licence and specimen page, and installed=true when it is already available (downloaded into the Kadr data folder or bundled with the app). Use it to pick a font by mood, then call font.install {id} and text.update {font: id}. Read-only and offline: nothing is downloaded. Filters: query (name, id or note), category, cyrillic, installed.
UI: Inspector/Text/Font/More fonts.
Returns: {count, total, families:[{id, name, category, cyrillic, ukrainian? (after install), note, license, license_url, page_url, repo_path, variable, size_bytes, files:[{style, file, url, size_bytes}], installed, source?, font_id, job?{state, progress, error}}], categories, base_url, folders{downloaded, bundled[], system[]}}.

category.description: Only families of this style: sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace or pixel.

cyrillic.description: true = only families with Cyrillic letters (Ukrainian/Russian text); false = only Latin-only ones.

installed.description: true = only families that are already installed; false = only those that still need font.install.

query.description: Case-insensitive search in the family name, id and note, e.g. "script", "retro", "mono".

post.description:
Installs a font file from this computer into the Kadr data folder so it can be used in texts — "Import font file" in the Text → Font picker. Accepts TrueType (.ttf), OpenType (.otf) and collections (.ttc/.otc); the file is checked (it must parse and draw Latin, digit or Cyrillic glyphs; web fonts .woff/.woff2 and CFF2 variable fonts are rejected with a hint) and copied — the original stays where it is. The family name inside the font becomes the font id ("My Brand Sans" → "my_brand_sans"); importing the other styles of the same family (Bold, Italic…) adds them to that family. The category (sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace, pixel) is inferred from the font unless given. Publishes fonts.changed. Make sure the font's licence allows the use you plan.
UI: Inspector/Text/Font/Import font file.
Returns: {font_id, family, style, category, cyrillic, ukrainian, variable, path (the stored copy), replaced}.

category.description: Only families of this style: sans, serif, display, handwriting, monospace or pixel.

path.description: Absolute path of the .ttf/.otf/.ttc file to import.

replace.description: Replace an already imported file of the same family and style (or a catalogue install of that family).

post.description:
Downloads a font family from font.catalog into the Kadr data folder (<DataDir>/fonts/<id>/) so it can be used in any text — the Install button in the Text → Font picker. Fetches the family's font files and its OFL.txt licence over HTTPS from the google/fonts repository, checks every file (size limits, TrueType/OpenType signature, the font must draw), checks that the licence is the SIL Open Font License, then moves the folder into place atomically — a failed or interrupted download leaves nothing behind. Variable fonts get real Regular and Bold weights. Runs in the background and returns at once unless wait=true; progress arrives as font.progress events (state queued → downloading → verifying → installing → done | failed, with downloaded_bytes/total_bytes/progress), and fonts.changed when the font is ready. Afterwards use font_id with text.update {font}. An already installed family is not downloaded again (already_installed=true) unless force=true. Fails with not_found for unknown ids and not_available when the internet cannot be reached.
UI: Inspector/Text/Font/More fonts.
Returns: {started, already_installed, font_id, message, job{id, font_id, state, file, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress, error, hint}}.

example2.summary: Install Caveat and wait until it is ready

force.description: Download and reinstall even when the family is already installed.

wait.description: Block until the font is installed (or failed) instead of returning immediately.

post.description:
Deletes a font family that was installed with font.install or font.import (library.list kind=font category=Downloaded) from the Kadr data folder. Built-in, bundled and operating-system fonts cannot be removed here (conflict). Texts that use the removed font fall back to Go Sans until it is installed again (font.install restores catalogue fonts with the same id). Publishes fonts.changed.
UI: Inspector/Text/Font/Remove font.
Risk: delete — deletes data from disk and cannot be undone with edit.undo; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {font_id, family, dir}.

font_id.description: Font id of a downloaded/imported family, e.g. "montserrat".

post.description:
Re-reads every font folder — the Kadr data folder (downloaded/imported fonts), the folders bundled with the app (<exe dir>/fonts, Kadr.app/Contents/Resources/fonts on macOS, KADR_FONTS_DIR) and, with system=true, the operating system's font folders — so fonts copied there while Kadr runs appear in library.list kind=font without a restart. Returns the number of families per source and the folders that were scanned. Publishes fonts.changed.
UI: Inspector/Text/Font/Rescan.
Returns: {downloaded, bundled, system, total (family counts), folders{downloaded, bundled[], system[]}}.

system.description: Also rescan the operating-system font folders (slower; a few seconds with thousands of fonts).

post.description:
Adds (or updates) a keyframe of one animatable property — the diamond button next to a slider in the CapCut inspector. Once a property has two or more keyframes its value is interpolated between them; before the first / after the last keyframe it holds that keyframe's value. If a keyframe of the same property already exists within half a frame of time_us it is updated instead of duplicated. value defaults to the property's current (interpolated) value at that time, so calling it without value just 'pins' what is on screen. Values use the stored units: transform.x/y in canvas fractions (-2..2), transform.scale as multiplier (0.01..4), transform.rotation in degrees (-360..360), opacity 0..1, volume as LINEAR gain 0..10 (1 = 0 dB, 0.5 ≈ -6 dB; gain = 10^(dB/20)), adjust.* -1..1 (sharpen, fade, grain and lut_intensity 0..1; adjust.hue -1..1 = -180..180 degrees; adjust.shine -1..1 local contrast), filter.intensity 0..1 (strength of the clip's or filter segment's filter — CapCut's filter Intensity keyframe). easing shapes the motion from this keyframe to the next one. While a property has keyframes, segment.set_transform / set_opacity / set_volume / set_adjust record their value as a keyframe at the playhead instead of changing the static value. Picture properties need a video, photo, sticker or text segment; volume needs sound; adjust.* needs a video/photo clip or adjustment segment; filter.intensity needs a segment that has a filter (a clip after filter.apply, or a filter-track segment).
UI: Inspector/◇ keyframe button.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, keyframe: {property, time_us, timeline_us, value, easing}, keyframes: all keyframes of that property}.

example1.summary: Zoom from 100% to 150% over the first 2 seconds (two calls)

example3.summary: Pin the current opacity at the playhead

example4.summary: Duck the volume to -12 dB at 5 s

example5.summary: Fade a filter in: intensity 0 at the start (then 1 at 1 s with a second call)

example6.summary: Animate a hue sweep: +90° at 2 s

easing.description: Interpolation from this keyframe to the next: linear (default for new keyframes), ease_in, ease_out or ease_in_out. Omit to keep the easing of an existing keyframe.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

time_us.description: Keyframe time relative to the segment start (0 = first frame of the clip). Defaults to the playhead position minus the segment start; the playhead must then be over the segment. Unit: microseconds.

value.description: Value at this keyframe in the property's stored unit (see description). Defaults to the current value at time_us.

post.description:
Removes all keyframes of a segment, or only those of one property / group ("transform", "adjust"). Each property keeps the value it shows at the playhead (or at the segment start when the playhead is outside the segment) as its new static value. Clearing a segment without keyframes is a no-op that still succeeds.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, removed: number of keyframes removed, keyframes: remaining keyframes}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

property.description: Only clear this property or group ("transform", "adjust"). Omit to clear every keyframe of the segment.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Lists the keyframes of a segment sorted by time, optionally filtered by property or group ("transform", "adjust"). Each item has time_us relative to the segment start and timeline_us on the timeline. Also returns the list of keyframeable properties that apply to this segment type.
Returns: {segment_id, start_us, duration_us, keyframes: [{property, time_us, timeline_us, value, easing}], properties: keyframeable property names for this segment}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

property.description: Only list this property or group ("transform", "adjust").

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Removes the keyframe(s) at one time — clicking a filled diamond in the inspector. time_us defaults to the playhead (relative to the segment start) and matches keyframes within half a frame. With property only that property's keyframe is removed; property may also be a group ("transform", "adjust" or "filter"); without property the keyframes of every property at that time are removed. When a property loses its last keyframe it keeps the value it had at that time, so the picture does not jump. Returns not_found when nothing matches.
UI: Inspector/◆ keyframe button.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, removed: number of keyframes removed, keyframes: remaining keyframes of the segment}.

example2.summary: Remove every keyframe at the playhead
