property.description: Property (or group "transform"/"adjust"/"filter") whose keyframe to remove. Omit to remove the keyframes of all properties at that time.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

time_us.description: Keyframe time relative to the segment start (0 = first frame of the clip). Defaults to the playhead position minus the segment start; the playhead must then be over the segment. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Returns one library item with all its details: name, categories, description, default parameters (effect intensity/speed, filter intensity, voice-effect ffmpeg filter), default duration, the full TextStyle of a text template, or the available styles of a font. Use it to inspect an id found in library.list or stored in a project (e.g. segment.transition_out.type). Animated items include preview {url, frames, fps, width, height} (the hover sprite strip); call library.preview to look at the motion as one image.
UI: Library.
Returns: The item: {kind, id, name, category, categories, description, anim_kind?, default_duration_us?, params?, style?, thumbnail, preview?}.

kind.description: Library kind of the item (see library.list).

post.description:
Lists the built-in library of one kind — exactly what the left panel tabs show: transitions, video effects, colour filters, clip animations (In/Out/Combo/Loop), text templates (style presets), fonts (embedded Go fonts, fonts installed on this computer, fonts bundled with Kadr and fonts downloaded with font.install — see font.catalog), stickers and voice effects. Every item has a stable id to pass to the matching command (transition.set type, effect.add effect_id, filter.add filter_id, animation.set id, text.add template_id, text.update font, sticker.add sticker_id, segment.set_audio voice_effect), a display name, CapCut-style categories, default parameters/durations and a thumbnail path (GET it with the API token for a PNG preview rendered by the engine). Filter by category tab and/or a case-insensitive search query, like the search box in the panel. More kinds: sound_effect (sfx.add), caption_style (captions.set_style), text_effect (text.apply_effect), text_animation (text.set_glyph_animation), generated (media.generate preset_id). Effects carry params.schema — the named sliders accepted by effect.set_params ({id, label, min, max, default}); transitions list their direction/softness options (see transition.set and transition.get). Items that move (transitions, effects, filters, clip animations, animated text templates/word art, text animations, caption styles with word highlight, animated stickers and generated clips) also carry preview {url, frames, fps, width, height}: GET url for a JPEG sprite strip (frames side by side, one seamless loop) — the app's hover preview; items without it are static. To SEE how an item plays, call library.preview (a PNG contact sheet).
UI: Library.
Returns: {kind, categories: [category tab names in display order], total, items: [{kind, id, name, category, categories, description, anim_kind?, default_duration_us?, params?, style? (text templates), thumbnail, preview? {url, frames, fps, width, height}}]}.

category.description: Only items in this category tab (case-insensitive), e.g. "Trending", "Basic", "In", "Retro". The result's categories field lists valid values.

kind.description: Which library to list: transition, effect, filter, animation, text_template, font, sticker, voice_effect, sound_effect, caption_style, text_effect, text_animation or generated.

query.description: Case-insensitive search on the item name, id, categories and description (the panel's search box).

post.description:
Renders how a library item PLAYS as one PNG contact sheet (frames left to right, top to bottom) so an AI agent can see a transition, effect, filter, clip animation, animated text template, text animation, caption style highlight, animated sticker or animated generated clip before applying it. Uses the same engine and sample pictures as the hover previews of the app: transitions go from a sunny landscape (clip A, progress 0) to a night city (clip B, progress 1); effects run over time on the landscape (static effects such as vignette show a before/after divider); filters show a before/after divider; clip animations move a small clip on a dark stage (dashed outline = rest position); text kinds render sample text. Static items (fonts, voice effects, non-animated templates/word art/stickers) return their thumbnail as a single tile with animated=false. Every item that animates has a preview field in library.list / library.get (the app's hover sprite: GET preview.url for a JPEG strip). Read-only.
UI: Library.
Returns: {kind, id, name, animated, frames, columns, rows, tile_width, tile_height, width, height, phases[] (0..1 position of each tile in the preview loop), times_us[] (the same in microseconds), loop_us (length of the hover loop), preview? ({url, frames, fps, width, height} of the JPEG sprite), png_base64, note (what the tiles show for this kind)}.

columns.description: Tiles per row; rows are added as needed.

frames.description: Number of moments (tiles) to render; more tiles show the motion in finer steps.

kind.description: Library kind of the item: transition, effect, filter, animation, text_template, text_effect, text_animation, caption_style, sticker, generated (others are static).

tile_width.description: Width of each tile; the height follows the preview's aspect ratio (16:9 for most kinds, square for stickers and text animations). Unit: pixels.

post.description:
Generates a low-resolution proxy of a video (540p on the short side, H.264, short GOP for fast seeking) in the background, like CapCut's "Create proxy". The player and timeline decode the proxy instead of the original for smooth preview of 4K/HEVC footage; export always uses the original. The command returns immediately with status "started" (or "running" if a job is already in progress, or "ready" when a proxy for the current file already exists — then proxy_path is set right away). Progress is published as media.import.progress events with stage "proxy"; when done the material's proxy_path is saved and a media.ready event with stage "proxy" is sent. Only videos can have proxies.
UI: Library/Media/Create proxy.
Returns: {material_id, status: "started"|"running"|"ready", proxy_path}.

force.description: Regenerate the proxy even if one already exists for this file.

post.description:
Removes a material from the project's media library (Media panel → right-click → Delete). Like CapCut, every timeline segment that uses it is removed from all tracks too: on the main track with the magnet on, the following clips shift left to close the gap; a transition leading into a removed clip is dropped; overlay/audio tracks that become empty are removed (the main track is kept). The file on disk is never touched and cached thumbnails are kept so edit.undo restores everything instantly.
UI: Library/Media/Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {deleted: true, material_id, removed_segments: [segment ids], removed_tracks: [track ids]}.

post.description:
Creates a procedural media file — a background, texture, pattern, test card or countdown drawn by the engine itself (no stock footage, nothing downloaded) — and adds it to the project as a normal material, like CapCut's generated/stock backgrounds but fully original and offline. Still kinds (solid colours, still gradients, grids, checkers, stripes, textures, patterns, colour bars without tone) are written as a PNG (material type photo, duration 0: it can be stretched to any length on the timeline); banner and frame are PNGs with a transparent background meant for an overlay track; kinds that move (speed > 0, noise, countdowns, timers) or make sound (colour-bar tone, countdown beeps) are rendered frame by frame and encoded to an H.264 MP4 of duration_us (material type video). Files go to <project>/cache/generated/ and are reused when the same kind, params, size, duration and fps are asked again (cached = true; the existing material is returned instead of a duplicate). Pick a ready-made look with preset_id (ids from library.list kind=generated, e.g. "sunset_gradient", "neon_floor", "countdown_5", "film_grain") — params then override single preset values — or give kind + params yourself. Size defaults to the project canvas; videos use the canvas fps (or 30) and even pixel sizes. With add_to_timeline the new material is also placed in the same undo step, exactly like timeline.segment.add: on the main track at the clip boundary nearest at_us (magnet), or appended to the end of the main track when at_us is omitted; track_id / new_track choose another track (e.g. an overlay track for grain, confetti, light leaks, film dust, banners or frames on top of a clip — light_leak and film_dust are drawn on black for segment.set_blend mode screen). Moving backgrounds with a loop param (mesh, aurora, lava, plasma, bokeh, particles, light_leak) repeat seamlessly every loop seconds, which is also their default length. Rendering runs while the command executes (typically 2-10 s for 5 s of 1080p video); duration_us is limited to 60 s — for longer backgrounds use a still kind or add the clip several times. Undo removes the material (and the placed clip); the cached file stays on disk. Kinds: • solid — a flat colour card (PNG) — backgrounds, chroma-key plates, fade cards. Params: color (color, default "#000000"): Fill colour.. • gradient — a smooth linear or radial colour gradient (PNG, or a flowing video when speed > 0). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FF7A59","#7B2FF7"]): Colour stops, evenly spaced, from start to end (2-6).; type (enum linear|radial, default "linear"): linear = along angle; radial = from the centre outwards.; angle (number -360..360, default 135): Direction of a linear gradient in degrees: 0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Colour flow speed in back-and-forth cycles per 10 seconds. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • color_bars — a test card of vertical colour bars (PNG, or a video with a sine tone when tone = true). Params: style (enum classic|rainbow|retro, default "classic"): classic = broadcast-style 75% bars with a lower calibration row; rainbow = 12 hues over a grey step wedge; retro = muted 70s palette.; tone (boolean, default false): Add a continuous sine test tone (the output becomes a video with sound).; tone_hz (number 100..8000, default 1000): Frequency of the test tone in hertz.. • noise — film grain, TV static, paper and soft cloudy textures from value noise (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#808080"): Base colour; the noise brightens and darkens it.; color2 (color): Optional second colour: the noise blends between color and color2 instead of brightening/darkening.; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): Strength (contrast) of the noise.; scale (number 1..400, default 1): Grain size in pixels at 1080p height: 1-2 = fine grain/static, 100+ = soft clouds.; octaves (integer 1..5, default 1): Layers of finer detail added on top (fractal noise); 3-4 for paper and smoke.; monochrome (boolean, default true): Same noise in R, G and B (false = coloured RGB noise).; speed (number 0..4, default 1): How fast the noise changes: 1 = 24 new grain patterns per second (soft noise drifts smoothly). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 1): Random seed: another number gives another pattern.. • shapes — circles, rounded squares, triangles and rings drifting over a colour (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: shape (enum mixed|circle|square|triangle|ring, default "mixed"): Which shapes to draw.; count (integer 1..80, default 18): Number of shapes.; colors (colors, 1-8, default ["#FF5C8A","#FFD23F","#3EC1D3","#9B5DE5","#00F5D4"]): Shape colours, used in turn.; background (color, default "#16161D"): Background colour.; size (number 0.01..0.5, default 0.07): Average shape radius as a fraction of the frame height.; opacity (number 0.1..1, default 0.9): Shape opacity.; speed (number 0..5, default 1): Drift speed (1 = calm). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 7): Random seed for positions, sizes and directions.. • countdown — a numeric countdown (from N to 1, one number per second by default) as a video. Params: from (integer 1..60, default 5): First number; the clip counts down to 1. Default length = from seconds.; style (enum ring|plain|film, default "ring"): ring = number inside an emptying progress ring; plain = big fading numbers; film = projector-leader look with a sweeping wedge and crosshair (use a light background).; background (color, default "#111114"): Background colour.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the numbers (and of the film-style circles).; accent (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Colour of the progress ring / sweeping wedge.; beep (boolean, default false): Add a short beep at every number (the video gets a sound track).. • grid — a line grid — flat (blueprint, graph paper) or a perspective floor running to the horizon (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum flat|perspective, default "flat"): flat = square grid; perspective = floor grid towards a horizon with a sky above.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Line colour.; background (color, default "#101018"): Background (floor) colour.; color2 (color): Sky colour at the top of a perspective grid (default: the background colour).; cells (integer 2..64, default 12): Number of grid cells across the frame width.; thickness (number 0.5..20, default 2): Line thickness in pixels at 1080p height.; glow (boolean, default false): Soft neon glow around the lines (and on the horizon).; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Scroll speed in cells per second (towards the viewer). 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • checker — a two-colour checkerboard, optionally rotated and scrolling (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): First square colour.; color2 (color, default "#D9D9E0"): Second square colour.; cells (integer 2..128, default 8): Number of squares across the frame width.; angle (number -180..180, default 0): Rotation of the pattern in degrees.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Diagonal scroll speed in squares per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • stripes — diagonal or straight stripes in 2-6 colours, optionally moving like a barber pole (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FFD23F","#1B1B1F"]): Stripe colours, repeated in order.; width (number 0.005..0.5, default 0.06): Width of one stripe as a fraction of the frame height.; angle (number -180..180, default 45): Stripe direction in degrees: 0 = vertical stripes, 90 = horizontal.; speed (number 0..10, default 0): Movement in stripes per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • mesh — a soft modern mesh gradient: colour clouds blended into each other, slowly drifting in a seamless loop (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FF9A8B","#FF6A88","#FF99AC","#FAD0C4","#A18CD1"]): Colours of the blended clouds (2-6).; softness (number 0..1, default 0.5): 0 = distinct colour patches, 1 = very soft, misty blending.; grain (number 0..0.3, default 0.04): Fine film grain on top (0 = clean).; speed (number 0..3, default 1): How far the colour clouds drift (1 = calm). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 3): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • aurora — northern lights: glowing curtains of light waving over a starry night sky (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-4, default ["#00FFA3","#00C2FF","#B026FF"]): Curtain colours from the bottom edge of the light upwards.; background (color, default "#040714"): Night sky colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#0A2A3C"): Sky colour near the horizon (bottom).; stars (boolean, default true): Twinkling stars in the sky.; landscape (boolean, default true): Dark mountain and forest silhouette along the bottom.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Wave speed of the curtains. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 5): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • lava — glossy blobs that rise, sink, merge and split like a lava lamp (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 1-4, default ["#FFB000","#FF3D6E","#B5179E"]): Blob colours from top to bottom of the frame.; background (color, default "#1B0B2E"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#3A0D4F"): Background colour at the bottom.; count (integer 2..16, default 7): Number of blobs.; size (number 0.04..0.3, default 0.13): Blob radius as a fraction of the frame height.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Rise/sink speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 11): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • plasma — a retro demo-scene plasma: interfering colour waves cycling through a palette (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#120458","#7A04EB","#FF00A0","#FE75FE","#00F0FF"]): Palette the waves cycle through.; scale (number 0.3..6, default 1.5): Wave density: higher = more, smaller ripples.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Wave speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 2): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • bokeh — out-of-focus light discs drifting and twinkling over a dark gradient, like city lights behind a lens (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 1-6, default ["#FFD27A","#FF9F5A","#FFF2C4"]): Light colours.; background (color, default "#120E1C"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#2B1B2E"): Background colour at the bottom.; count (integer 4..150, default 36): Number of light discs.; size (number 0.01..0.3, default 0.08): Average disc radius as a fraction of the frame height.; softness (number 0..1, default 0.35): Edge softness: 0 = crisp discs, 1 = very blurry.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Drift speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 8): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • particles — light particles: floating dust, fireflies, falling snow, twinkling stars or rising embers (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum dust|fireflies|snow|stars|embers, default "dust"): dust = slow glowing motes; fireflies = wandering pulsing green-gold lights; snow = flakes falling with a sway; stars = twinkling starfield; embers = sparks rising and flickering.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Particle colour (fireflies and embers tint it warmer).; background (color, default "#0B0F1A"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color): Optional background colour at the bottom (vertical gradient).; count (integer 10..800, default 160): Number of particles.; size (number 0.2..5, default 1): Particle size multiplier.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Movement speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 4): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • light_leak — film light leaks, burns, prism streaks and lens flares on black — put it on an overlay track with the Screen (or Add) blend mode (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum leak|burn|prism|flare, default "leak"): leak = soft warm glows drifting in from the edges; burn = hot film burn flaring from one side; prism = rainbow streaks sweeping across; flare = lens flare with a moving source, streak and ghost rings.; colors (colors, 1-5, default ["#FF3D00","#FF8A00","#FFC14D"]): Light colours (prism uses a rainbow when only defaults are given).; intensity (number 0.2..1.5, default 1): Brightness of the light.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Movement speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 6): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 9): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • film_dust — old-film dirt on black: dust specks, hairs and vertical scratches flickering every frame — use the Screen blend mode on top of a clip (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the dirt.; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): How much dirt.; speed (number 0..2, default 1): 1 = new dirt 12 times per second, like a projector. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 6): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • texture — a still material texture: paper, kraft paper, grunge wall, concrete, canvas, denim, marble, watercolour paper or wood (PNG). Params: style (enum paper|kraft|grunge|concrete|canvas|denim|marble|watercolor|wood, default "paper"): Material to imitate.; color (color): Base colour (default depends on the style).; color2 (color): Accent colour: fibres, stains, veins, watercolour blooms or grain (default depends on the style).; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): Strength of the texture detail.; scale (number 0.25..4, default 1): Size of the texture features.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 7): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • pattern — a decorative repeating pattern — memphis, waves, polka dots, halftone, terrazzo, chevron, honeycomb, gingham, scales, dot grid, isometric cubes or triangle mosaic (PNG, or a slowly scrolling video when speed > 0). Params: style (enum memphis|waves|dots|halftone|terrazzo|chevron|honeycomb|gingham|scales|dot_grid|cubes|triangles, default "memphis"): Pattern design.; colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FFF4E6","#FF6B6B","#4ECDC4","#FFD93D","#6A4C93"]): Background colour first, then the pattern colours.; scale (number 2..64, default 8): Pattern repeats across the frame width.; angle (number -180..180, default 0): Rotation of the pattern in degrees.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Diagonal scroll speed in repeats per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 12): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • timer — a styled countdown video from N to 1 — flip clock, neon ring, progress bar, vanishing dots or pop-art bursts. Params: from (integer 1..60, default 5): First number; the clip counts down to 1. Default length = from seconds.; style (enum flip|neon|bar|dots|pop, default "flip"): flip = split-flap clock cards that flip every second; neon = glowing ring and digits; bar = big number over a shrinking progress bar; dots = a ring of dots that go out one by one; pop = the number punches in over a coloured starburst.; background (color, default "#121216"): Background colour.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the numbers.; accent (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (cards, ring, bar, dots, bursts).; beep (boolean, default false): Add a short beep at every number (the video gets a sound track).. • banner — a text-free banner shape on a transparent background — lower third, pill, tab, ribbon, glass panel, news bar or brush stroke — to put your own text on (PNG with alpha). Params: style (enum lower_third|pill|tab|ribbon|glass|news|brush, default "lower_third"): Banner design.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Main panel colour.; color2 (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (bars, tags, ribbon ends, icon slot).; position (enum bottom|center|top, default "bottom"): Vertical position in the frame.; width (number 0.2..1, default 0.6): Banner width as a fraction of the frame width.. • frame — a border overlay with a transparent centre — film strip, neon, instant photo, vignette, torn paper, viewfinder, rounded, postage stamp or double line (PNG with alpha). Params: style (enum film|neon|polaroid|vignette|torn|viewfinder|rounded|stamp|double, default "rounded"): Frame design.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Main frame colour (vignette: the shadow colour).; color2 (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (neon glow, viewfinder REC dot, inner line).; thickness (number 0.01..0.25, default 0.05): Border thickness as a fraction of the frame height..
UI: Library/Stickers/Generated.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {material_id, material, kind, preset_id?, params (all values incl. defaults), output: "png"|"mp4", path, width, height, duration_us (0 for a still picture), fps?, has_audio, cached, track_id?, segment_id?, segment?} — the generated material, and the placed clip when add_to_timeline is true.

name.description: Display name of the new material in the Media panel. Default: the preset name, or the kind title (e.g. "Gradient").

new_track.description: With add_to_timeline: put the clip on a brand-new overlay track (e.g. grain or confetti over existing clips).

params.description: Kind-specific settings, e.g. {"colors": ["#FF5E62", "#FFD86F"], "angle": 90} for a gradient or {"from": 3, "beep": true} for a countdown. Colours are "#RRGGBB"; numbers outside their range are rejected. Omitted keys use the defaults listed per kind in the description.

preset_id.description: Ready-made generator from library.list kind=generated (e.g. "sunset_gradient", "aurora_flow", "paper", "neon_floor", "countdown_5", "bars_tone"). Sets kind and params; params you also pass override single values.

post.description:
Returns one material with everything known about it: the probed metadata, whether the file is missing, every timeline segment that uses it (track, segment id, timeline and source ranges), which background assets are ready (thumbnail, waveform, filmstrip, proxy) and the URLs of its preview endpoints. Use it to check a file after media.import or before deleting media that is in use.
Returns: {…Material, in_use, use_count, missing, thumbnail_url, frame_url?, waveform_url?, usage: [{track_id, track_type, segment_id, start_us, end_us, source_start_us, source_duration_us}], assets: {thumbnail, waveform, filmstrip, proxy, proxy_running}}.

material_id.description: ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Imports video, photo and audio files into the project's media library — the Import button of the Media panel (left panel → Media → Local), the native file dialog, or dropping files onto the window. Every file is probed with ffprobe: type (video / photo / audio, detected from the streams and extension; animated GIFs are videos, single-frame GIFs are photos), duration (photos get 0 because they can be stretched to any length), display width/height (already swapped for 90°/270° rotated phone videos), rotation, frame rate, video/audio codecs, sample rate, channels and file size. A folder path imports the supported media files directly inside it (not recursive, max 500). Files already in the project (same path) are not imported twice: they are reported in duplicates with their existing material_id. Files that cannot be imported (missing, relative path, not a media file) are reported in errors without failing the whole import; the command only fails when nothing at all could be imported. Importing does NOT place anything on the timeline — call timeline.segment.add with the returned material ids for that. After the command returns, thumbnails, the filmstrip and audio waveforms are generated in the background: watch the media.import.progress events and media.ready (data.stage = "assets") on the event stream; the thumbnail/frame/waveform endpoints also work immediately (they generate on demand).
UI: Library/Media/Import. Hotkey: Ctrl+I.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {materials: [Material], duplicates: [{path, material_id}], errors: [{path, code, message}]}. Material = {id, type (video|photo|audio), name, path, duration_us, width, height, rotation, fps, video_codec, has_audio, audio_codec, sample_rate, channels, size_bytes, imported_at}.

example1.summary: Import a clip and a song

example2.summary: Import every media file of a folder

paths.description: Absolute paths of files (or folders) on the machine running Kadr, e.g. ["C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\clip.mp4"]. Surrounding quotes and file:// URLs are accepted.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Lists the materials (imported files) of the project in import order — the cards of the Media panel. Each item has the full probed metadata plus live information: in_use/use_count (how many timeline segments use it; the UI shows an "Added" mark), missing (the file is no longer on disk — fix it with media.relink) and the relative URLs of its thumbnail, source frame and waveform endpoints (append ?token=… or send the API token). Use the ids with timeline.segment.add to place media on the timeline.
UI: Library/Media.
Returns: Array of {…Material, in_use, use_count, missing, thumbnail_url, frame_url?, waveform_url?}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive filter on the material name (the Media panel search box).

type.description: Only return materials of this type (the Media panel's type filter). Omit for all imported media.

post.description:
Points a material at another file — CapCut's "Link media" for files that were moved or renamed (the card shows a missing badge). The new file is probed and must be the same kind (video, photo or audio); the material keeps its id, so every timeline clip using it follows automatically. Metadata (duration, size, codecs…) is refreshed, the old proxy is dropped and thumbnails/waveform/filmstrip are regenerated in the background. If the new file is shorter than ranges used on the timeline, those segment ids are listed in warnings (the clips are left unchanged; trim them with timeline.segment.trim).
UI: Library/Media/Relink.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {material: Material, warnings: [{segment_id, message}]}.

material_id.description: ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import.

path.description: Absolute path of the replacement file on the machine running Kadr.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Changes the display name of a material in the Media panel (right-click → Rename). Only the name shown in Kadr changes — the file on disk keeps its name. Timeline clips show the new name as their label.
UI: Library/Media/Rename.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated Material.

material_id.description: ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import.

name.description: New display name; leading/trailing spaces are removed, must not be empty (max 255 characters).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Lists every timeline segment that uses a material, on all tracks (main track, overlays, audio tracks). An empty list means the material is only in the media library. CapCut warns before deleting media that is in use; call this first to know which clips media.delete would remove.
Returns: {material_id, count, segments: [{track_id, track_type, segment_id, start_us, end_us, source_start_us, source_duration_us}]}.

material_id.description: ID of the material (imported media item), e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from media.list or media.import.

post.description:
Pauses playback, leaving the playhead where playback reached (pressing Pause under the player). Pausing when nothing is playing is harmless and just returns the current state. Publishes a playback.state event {playing:false, time_us} and moves the playhead (playhead.moved). Use playback.seek afterwards to put the playhead at an exact time.
UI: Player/Pause.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Starts playback from the playhead (or from from_us), like pressing Play under the player. If the playhead is at the end of the timeline, playback starts over from 0. While playing, the engine advances the playhead about 10 times per second (playhead.moved events, source "playback") and stops by itself at the end; the editor shows the composited stream (/stream) with sound (/audio). Publishes a playback.state event {playing, time_us}. Playing an empty timeline does nothing and returns playing=false. Playback state is not saved in the project and is not undoable.
UI: Player/Play.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

from_us.description: Optional start time. Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Moves the playhead to time_us — clicking or dragging on the timeline ruler. The player then shows the frame at that time (render it yourself with preview.frame). If playback is running it continues from the new position (a playback.state event with the new time_us is published). Times are not clamped to the timeline length (CapCut lets the playhead sit past the last clip); negative values become 0. Publishes playhead.moved. Not undoable; does not modify the project.
UI: Timeline/Ruler click.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

time_us.description: Target playhead time in microseconds (2.5 s = 2500000). Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Returns whether the project is playing, the current playhead time (advancing in real time while playing), the timeline duration and the project frame rate. Use it to poll playback started by the user or another client, or subscribe to playback.state / playhead.moved events on the WebSocket instead.
UI: Player.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Moves the playhead exactly one frame (1/fps of the project frame rate, e.g. 33333 µs at 30 fps) backward or forward — the Left/Right arrow keys. The playhead is first snapped to the frame grid, so repeated steps land on frame boundaries. Pauses playback if it is running. Stepping stops at 0 and at the end of the timeline. Publishes playhead.moved.
UI: Keyboard. Hotkey: Left/Right.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Toggles between playing and paused — the Space key and the round play button under the player. When starting, playback begins at the playhead (from 0 if the playhead is at the end) and the engine advances the playhead in real time until the end of the timeline. When pausing, the playhead stays where playback reached. Publishes playback.state {playing, time_us}; every connected editor and API client sees the change.
UI: Player/Play button. Hotkey: Space.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Applies a preset from the user's kit to a clip, like clicking a card in "My kit" with a clip selected. Only the part stored in the preset changes (e.g. a filter preset sets only the filter). This is one undo step. Clips on locked tracks are rejected (conflict); a preset of the wrong kind for the clip fails with invalid_argument and a hint. Kinds and their targets: text_style → text clips (content, word timings and animations of the target are kept); adjust → video, photo and adjustment clips; filter → video, photo, sticker and filter clips; effect → video, photo and sticker clips (merged into the clip's effect list, same id replaced) or effect clips (first effect); transition → the LEFT clip of two touching clips on a video track (duration clamped to half of the shorter clip); animation → video, photo, sticker and text clips (In/Out replace Combo and vice versa, durations fit into the clip; loop and per-letter parts only for text).
UI: Library/My kit/Apply.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {preset_id, kind, name, segment_id, segment: the updated segment, notes: adjustments made to fit the clip (e.g. a clamped transition duration)}.

preset_id.description: ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Clip to apply the preset to (project.get → tracks[].segments[].id).

post.description:
Removes a preset from the user's kit (My kit → card → Delete). Clips that already use the look keep it — presets are copied into clips when applied, never linked. This cannot be undone with edit.undo because the kit is not part of a project.
UI: Library/My kit/Delete.
Risk: delete — deletes data from disk and cannot be undone with edit.undo; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {deleted: preset id, kind}.

post.description:
Returns one preset of the user's kit with all captured values (data.text_style, data.adjust, data.filter, data.effects, data.transition or data.animations depending on kind), so an AI agent can inspect what presets.apply would change before applying it.
UI: Library/My kit.
Returns: The preset: {id, kind, name, summary, source, created_at, updated_at, data}.

preset_id.description: ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list.

post.description:
Lists the presets saved in the user's kit ("My kit" tab), newest first, optionally filtered by kind and by a case-insensitive name/summary search. Use the returned ids with presets.apply, presets.rename and presets.delete. counts reports how many presets exist per kind (before filtering), handy for building the kind navigation. The kit is per user, not per project.
UI: Library/My kit.
Returns: {presets: [preset…], total: number returned, kinds: all valid kinds, counts: {kind: n}}.

kind.description: Only presets of this kind (text_style, adjust, filter, effect, transition, animation).

query.description: Case-insensitive text matched against the preset name and summary.

post.description:
Renames a preset in the user's kit (My kit → card → Rename). The name is trimmed and may be at most 80 characters; it does not need to be unique. Renaming changes nothing in any project.
UI: Library/My kit/Rename.
Returns: The renamed preset.

name.description: New name shown in My kit (1–80 characters).

preset_id.description: ID of a saved preset ("pst_…"). Get it from presets.list.

post.description:
Saves part of a clip's look as a reusable preset in the user's kit ("My kit" in the left library panel, the "Add to kit" buttons in the inspector). The preset is stored per user in <DataDir>/presets.json, so it is available in every project. kind decides what is captured from segment_id: text_style copies the whole text look (font, size, colour, stroke, shadow, box, glow, gradient fill, extrude, curve, word-art effect, caption highlight) but not the words; adjust copies all colour adjustments; filter, effect, transition and animation copy those settings. Fails with invalid_argument when the clip has nothing of that kind (e.g. no filter). The project is not modified, so this is not an undo step. Re-apply with presets.apply. Kinds and their targets: text_style → text clips (content, word timings and animations of the target are kept); adjust → video, photo and adjustment clips; filter → video, photo, sticker and filter clips; effect → video, photo and sticker clips (merged into the clip's effect list, same id replaced) or effect clips (first effect); transition → the LEFT clip of two touching clips on a video track (duration clamped to half of the shorter clip); animation → video, photo, sticker and text clips (In/Out replace Combo and vice versa, durations fit into the clip; loop and per-letter parts only for text).
UI: Inspector/Add to kit.
Returns: The saved preset: {id, kind, name, summary, source (clip type it came from), created_at, updated_at, data: {text_style|adjust|filter|effects|transition|animations}}.

example3.summary: Save a transition with an automatic name

from_segment_id.description: Alias of segment_id (accepted for compatibility); segment_id wins when both are set.

kind.description: What to capture: text_style (look of a text clip), adjust (colour adjustments incl. HSL/curves/LUT), filter (filter id + intensity), effect (the clip's video effects with their parameters), transition (the transition after the clip), animation (In/Out/Combo plus text loop and per-letter animations).

name.description: Name shown in My kit (max 80 characters). Default: "<Kind> <n>", e.g. "Text style 3".

project_id.description: Project that contains the clip to capture (from project.list).

segment_id.description: Clip to capture the look from (project.get → tracks[].segments[].id). Required unless from_segment_id is given.

post.description:
Renders several evenly spaced frames of the project into one PNG grid (a contact sheet) so an AI agent can review the whole edit — pacing, cuts, text and overlays — in a single image instead of calling preview.frame many times. Frames are sampled at the centre of `count` equal slices of [start_us, end_us) (default: the whole timeline) and laid out left-to-right, top-to-bottom; times_us lists the time of each tile in that order. Uses the same renderer as the player and export. Read-only.
UI: Player.
Returns: {width, height, columns, rows, tile_width, tile_height, times_us[], png_base64, warnings?}.

example2.summary: Six frames of the first 10 seconds

columns.description: Number of tiles per row; rows are added as needed.

end_us.description: End of the sampled range. Defaults to the end of the last segment. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

start_us.description: Start of the sampled range. Defaults to 0 (timeline start). Unit: microseconds.

tile_width.description: Width of each tile; the tile height follows the canvas aspect ratio. Unit: pixels.

post.description:
Renders the composited picture of the project at one timeline time — exactly what the player shows and what export will contain, because the same renderer is used: every visible track in order (main video, overlays, stickers, text, then filter/effect/adjustment tracks applied to everything below them), transforms, crop, opacity, blend modes, masks, chroma key, filters, adjustments, effects, animations, keyframes and transitions. Use it after edits to SEE the result. Returns the frame as base64 PNG plus `url`, the binary endpoint GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/frame (add the API token as Authorization header or ?token=; supports &w=, &h= and &format=png|jpeg). time_us defaults to the playhead; times past the end show only the canvas background. The height follows the canvas aspect ratio. Missing or undecodable media is skipped and listed in `warnings`. Read-only: the project and playhead are not changed.
UI: Player.
Returns: {width, height, time_us, png_base64, url, warnings?, note}: png_base64 is the PNG file encoded as base64; url is the path of the same frame on the /frame endpoint (JPEG by default).

example1.summary: Look at the frame 2 seconds into the video

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

time_us.description: Timeline time to render (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

width.description: Output width in pixels; the height is derived from the canvas aspect ratio (640 → 640x360 for 16:9). Unit: pixels.

post.description:
Returns where every visible clip is drawn on the canvas at one moment — the boxes the player uses for on-canvas selection, move/scale/rotate handles and snapping, and that agents can use to reason about composition (e.g. 'is the title over the face?'). Covers video, photo, sticker and text segments of visible tracks (effects, filters, adjustments and audio have no box). Coordinates are canvas pixels of Project.Canvas (e.g. 1920x1080), origin top-left, +y down. Each box gives the unrotated rectangle x, y, w, h, its centre cx, cy, rotation in degrees clockwise around the centre and the four rotated corners; w/h include crop, fit, transform.scale, keyframes and the current In/Out/Combo animation (exactly the renderer's placement); text boxes are the rendered text image (incl. stroke, shadow, box). transform holds the keyframed values without animation (what segment.set_transform edits) and base_w/base_h the size at scale 1, so a handle drag maps back to x = transform.x + dx/(canvas_width/2), scale = new_w/base_w. Boxes are in compositing order: the LAST box is on top, so hit-test from the end. Both clips of a running transition are listed. Read-only.
UI: Player.
Returns: {time_us, canvas_width, canvas_height, boxes:[{segment_id, track_id, track_type, type: video|photo|sticker|text, x, y, w, h, rotation, cx, cy, corners:[[x,y]×4 TL,TR,BR,BL], flip_h?, flip_v?, opacity, z, locked?, animated?, base_w, base_h, transform:{x, y, scale, rotation}, missing?}], warnings?}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

time_us.description: Timeline time to lay out (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Creates a new empty project, exactly like pressing "Create project" on the Home screen. Defaults match CapCut: 16:9 canvas at 1920x1080, 30 fps, black background, main-track magnet, auto snapping and linkage enabled. If name is omitted the project is named after today's date (MMDD).
UI: Home/Create project. Hotkey: Ctrl+N.
Returns: The full project object, including its new id.

fps.description: Project frame rate used for the timeline grid and export default. Unit: frames per second.

name.description: Project name shown on the Home screen and in the editor title bar.

ratio.description: Canvas aspect ratio. 9:16 is vertical (TikTok/Reels/Shorts), 16:9 is landscape (YouTube), 1:1 is square.

post.description:
Permanently deletes a project, its folder and its undo history. This cannot be undone. Same as Delete in the Home screen context menu. Imported media files on disk are NOT deleted; files inside the project's own folder (AI-generated videos, speech, generated media, mattes, caches) are. Before that, any other project that still uses one of those files (a copy made by an older version, media imported from this project's folder) gets its own copy in its own folder and its paths — undo history included — are repointed, so no other project loses media; kept_files / kept_for in the result report it.
UI: Home/Project menu/Delete.
Risk: delete — deletes data from disk and cannot be undone with edit.undo; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {deleted: true, project_id, kept_files?, kept_for?}: kept_files = files handed to the projects listed in kept_for (omitted when none).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Creates an independent copy of a project with a new id. The copy is named "<name> copy" unless a name is given. Same as Duplicate in the Home screen context menu. Imported media files stay where they are and are referenced, not copied. Files that live inside the project's own folder — AI-generated videos (ai-video/), speech (cache/tts/), generated media, background-removal mattes, proxies — are given to the copy (hard-linked when the disk allows it, so no extra space is used; copied otherwise) and the copy's paths point to them, so deleting either project never breaks the other and paid results never have to be made again.
UI: Home/Project menu/Duplicate.
Returns: The full new project object.

name.description: Name for the copy. Defaults to "<original name> copy".

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Returns the complete project state: canvas settings, all materials (imported media), every track with its segments (timeline clips) and all their properties, markers and timeline settings. Call this after edits to verify the result.
Returns: The full project object.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Returns every project in the local project library, most recently modified first — the same list shown on the Home screen. Each item contains the project id, name, canvas ratio and size, total duration and timestamps. Use the returned id as project_id for every other project command.
UI: Home/Projects.
Returns: Array of project summaries: {id, name, ratio, width, height, duration_us, created_at, modified_at}.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive filter on the project name (same as the Home screen search box).

post.description:
Changes the project name. Same as editing the name in the editor title bar or choosing Rename from a project's context menu on the Home screen. Renaming is not recorded in undo history (like CapCut).
UI: Home/Project menu/Rename.
Returns: The project summary after renaming.

name.description: New project name. Leading/trailing spaces are removed; must not be empty.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Changes the canvas (output frame) settings — the Ratio menu under the player and the canvas options in the inspector when nothing is selected. Changing the ratio recomputes width/height with the short side at 1080 px; existing clips keep their relative position and scale. Only the supplied fields change.
UI: Player/Ratio.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated canvas object.

background_blur.description: Blur strength 0..1 used when background_type is blur.

post.description:
Chooses the project's cover (thumbnail) frame — the Cover button at the start of the main track in CapCut. time_us is a TIMELINE time; the cover is the composited frame at that time (render it with GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/frame?t_us=<cover_us> or preview.frame). It must lie inside the project (0 ≤ time_us < project duration); an empty project has no frames and returns conflict. clear=true removes the choice so the first frame is used again. The value is stored in project.cover_us (null = first frame) and is one undo step. Moving or trimming clips later does not move the cover time.
UI: Timeline/Main track/Cover.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {cover_us: chosen time or null (first frame), duration_us: project duration}.

example1.summary: Use the frame at 2.5 s as the cover

clear.description: true = forget the chosen cover and use the first frame (time_us is ignored).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

time_us.description: Timeline time of the cover frame in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Required unless clear is true. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Lists the graphics adapters Kadr can render on (Settings → Rendering → GPU): index, name, vendor (nvidia, amd, intel, apple), backend (vulkan, d3d12, metal), device type (discrete, integrated, cpu = software, virtual), total VRAM in MB, the OS budget for Kadr when known, driver, recommended (the high-performance default), supported (has the features Kadr needs; note explains why not), selected (used with the current settings) and effective_cap_mb (the VRAM Kadr would allow itself on that adapter: min(vram_limit_mb or total, total − reserve_mb, OS budget)). The same physical GPU can appear once per backend. available=false means no usable GPU or no wgpu library was found — Kadr then renders on the CPU (same picture, slower) and reason/hint explain it. Use an index or name from here with render.settings.set adapter. Read-only.
UI: Settings/Rendering.
Returns: {available, adapters[{index, name, vendor, backend, device_type, driver?, vram_total_mb, vram_budget_mb?, recommended, supported, note?, selected, effective_cap_mb}], selected (index into adapters, -1 = CPU), mode, reason?, hint?}.

Returns how Kadr renders previews and exports (Settings → Rendering): mode (auto = GPU when a working adapter exists, otherwise CPU; gpu = GPU only; cpu = always the CPU reference renderer) and where it came from (settings, or env when KADR_RENDER_MODE overrides it), the chosen adapter ("" = recommended), vram_limit_mb (0 = automatic) and reserve_mb (VRAM kept free for Windows/macOS and other apps, default 512), the resulting effective_cap_mb on the selected adapter (it covers Kadr's own process — the wgpu device, its memory blocks, textures, caches, frames in flight — plus the hardware video decoders, 256 MB each out of a quarter of the cap, and an export's hardware encoder, 256 MB; below 1 GB nothing is left for them and video is decoded and encoded in software; Kadr keeps the process's real video memory under its part of the cap and gives memory back to the OS when idle), the adapter's total VRAM, vram_used_mb (textures and buffers Kadr allocated), vram_process_mb (what the OS charges to Kadr's process on the GPU right now, 0 = unknown), and active — the renderer actually in use (kind gpu|cpu, backend, device, device_cap_mb for the process, hw_decoders, hw_encoders, idle when the device was released after a pause and is re-created on the next frame, and reason when the CPU is used). Example: a 12 GB card with vram_limit_mb 12288 gives an effective cap of 11776 MB. Read-only.
UI: Settings/Rendering.
Returns: {mode, mode_source settings|env, adapter, vram_limit_mb, reserve_mb, effective_cap_mb (0 = unknown), vram_total_mb, vram_budget_mb?, vram_used_mb, vram_process_mb, gpu_available, selected_adapter?{…render.devices entry}, active{kind, backend?, device?, vendor?, vram_total_mb?, cap_mb?, device_cap_mb?, hw_decoders?, hw_encoders?, used_mb, process_mb, idle?, reason?}, saved{mode, adapter, vram_limit_mb, reserve_mb}, note?, warning?}.

Changes how Kadr renders and how much video memory it may use (Settings → Rendering) and saves it in settings.json "render". Only the given fields change. mode: auto (default; GPU when available, else CPU), gpu (refused when no usable GPU exists), cpu (always the CPU renderer). adapter: an index or name from render.devices (or a part of a name such as "RTX 3060"; numbers are indexes), "" = the recommended high-performance one. vram_limit_mb: how much VRAM Kadr may use, 0 = automatic (all of it minus reserve_mb); at least 256 and not more than the adapter's total VRAM (a round size like 12288 on a card the driver reports as 12115 MB is taken as "all of it"). reserve_mb: VRAM always left free for the system (default 512). The effective cap is min(vram_limit_mb or total, total − reserve_mb, OS budget): choosing 12288 on a 12 GB card leaves 512 MB for Windows and uses at most 11776 MB. Applies to the next frame or export, no restart; an export already running keeps its renderer. Picking a software adapter (device_type "cpu", e.g. Microsoft Basic Render Driver) is allowed for testing but returns a warning: it is many times slower than mode "cpu". App setting, not a project edit: not undoable. Calling it without changes returns the current settings with changed=false.
UI: Settings/Rendering.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: Same as render.settings.get plus changed (always present; false when nothing changed) and warning (e.g. the GPU is unavailable so the settings apply once it is, the chosen adapter is a slow software renderer, or KADR_RENDER_MODE overrides the mode).

example1.summary: Let Kadr use 12 GB (keeps 512 MB for Windows)

adapter.description: GPU to use: index or name from render.devices (a part such as "RTX 3060" is enough; a plain number is an index); "" = the recommended adapter. Omit to keep.

mode.description: "auto" (GPU when available, otherwise CPU), "gpu" (GPU only) or "cpu" (CPU reference renderer). Omit to keep.

reserve_mb.description: VRAM in MB always left free for the operating system and other apps; 0 = default 512. Unit: megabytes.

vram_limit_mb.description: Maximum VRAM Kadr may use in MB (1024 MB = 1 GB); 0 = automatic (total minus reserve_mb). At least 256 and at most the adapter's total VRAM. Unit: megabytes.

post.description:
Writes every stored secret — all API key pools (with labels, order and enabled state) and other provider secrets — to one password-protected backup file, so they can be moved to another computer or user (the OS encryption of the vault cannot travel) — Settings → Secrets → Export. The file is AES-256-GCM encrypted with a key derived from the password by PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600 000 iterations); without the password it is useless. Only run this when the user explicitly asks for a backup: anyone with the file and the password gets every key. The result reports counts only, never a key. Keys that cannot be decrypted on this computer are skipped (skipped > 0). An existing file is not replaced unless overwrite=true. App setting, not undoable.
UI: Settings/Secrets/Export.
Risk: secret — handles credentials; only the user runs it (agents never send, read or change keys and passwords).
Returns: {path, entries, keys, pools, bytes, skipped?} — counts only, never a secret.

overwrite.description: Replace the file when it already exists (default false: conflict error).

password.description: Password protecting the file, at least 8 characters. It is not stored anywhere; it is needed to import.

path.description: Absolute path of the backup file to write, e.g. C:\Users\me\Documents\kadr-secrets.json.

post.x-user-only: The key vault (status, export and import of every stored key) is managed only by the user in Kadr's Settings; AI agents never read, export or import it.

post.description:
Reads a backup written by secrets.export and stores its secrets in this computer's encrypted vault — Settings → Secrets → Import. mode "merge" (default) appends keys missing from each provider's pool (a key already present is counted in keys_duplicate and skipped; imported keys go to the end of the failover order with status unknown) and adds or overwrites other secrets; mode "replace" first deletes every secret stored here, then imports — use it only when the user asks to restore exactly the backup. A wrong password or a damaged file changes nothing (invalid_argument). Returns counts and the affected pools, never a key. App setting, not undoable.
UI: Settings/Secrets/Import.
Risk: secret — handles credentials; only the user runs it (agents never send, read or change keys and passwords).
Returns: {entries_added, entries_updated, keys_added, keys_duplicate, pools: ["kind/provider"], created (backup time), replaced}.

example1.summary: Restore keys on a new computer

mode.description: merge (default) keeps existing keys and adds new ones; replace deletes every stored secret first.

password.description: The password used when the backup was exported.

path.description: Absolute path of a backup file written by secrets.export.

post.x-user-only: The key vault (status, export and import of every stored key) is managed only by the user in Kadr's Settings; AI agents never read, export or import it.

post.description:
Describes where Kadr keeps API keys and how they are protected — Settings → Secrets. backend is "dpapi" (Windows Data Protection API: only this Windows user on this computer can decrypt), "keychain" (macOS login Keychain, service "Kadr") or "file" (Linux/other: a 0600 file, NOT encrypted — warning explains it). Lists every key pool (kind tts | video | llm …, provider id) with masked keys ("sk_…a1b2"), each key's status (ok, exhausted, invalid, rate_limited, unknown), last error, cooldown and remaining quota when the provider reports it, and how many keys are usable now. Never returns a secret value. Use the owning module's commands (tts.keys.*, videogen.keys.*, assistant settings) to add or remove keys; secrets.export / secrets.import back everything up.
UI: Settings/Secrets.
Returns: {backend, encrypted, location, warning?, entries, pools: count, keys: count, key_pools: [{kind, provider, usable, statuses{status: n}, keys: [{id, label, preview, status, disabled, usable, last_error, last_used, cooldown_until, quota{remaining, limit, unit, resets_at}, uses, failures}]}]} — masked previews only.

example1.summary: Where are my keys and do they work?

kind.description: Only pools of this kind ("tts", "video", "llm"); omit for all.

post.x-user-only: The key vault (status, export and import of every stored key) is managed only by the user in Kadr's Settings; AI agents never read, export or import it.

post.description:
Returns one segment with everything the inspector shows for it: the raw segment, its track, the kind (video, photo, audio, text, sticker, effect, filter, adjustment), the material, which property commands apply (capabilities), the keyframeable properties, and the evaluated values (transform, opacity, volume, adjustments and source time, keyframes interpolated) at time_us — by default at the playhead (clamped into the segment). Use it to check the effect of segment.* / keyframe.* commands.
UI: Inspector.
Returns: {segment, track_id, track_type, kind, material?, capabilities, keyframe_properties, time_us, evaluated, volume_db}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

time_us.description: Time relative to the segment start to evaluate keyframes at. Defaults to the playhead. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Resets one group of a segment's properties to CapCut's defaults — the ↺ buttons of the inspector sections. Groups: transform (position, scale 100%, rotation 0, flips + their keyframes), blend (opacity 100%, normal blend + opacity keyframes), crop, mask, chroma_key, background (canvas fill → project default), adjust (all colour adjustments, LUT, adjust.* keyframes), audio (0 dB, no fades, voice effect, noise reduction and normalisation off, volume keyframes), speed (1x, no curve, pitch off — the timeline length changes and the main track ripples like segment.set_speed), animation (in/out/combo/loop), keyframes (every keyframe) and all (every group that applies to this segment type). A specific group that does not apply (e.g. audio on a photo) is rejected with invalid_argument. Content (text, source range, filters, effects, transitions) is never touched.
UI: Inspector/Section/Reset.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, rippled_segments?} after the reset.

group.description: Which group of properties to reset; all resets every applicable group.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Returns every colour adjustment of a clip (or adjustment segment) to neutral — basic sliders (incl. hue, fade, grain, shine), all eight HSL bands and every tone curve — and removes its LUT and all adjust.* keyframes: the Reset button of CapCut's Adjustment tab. Filters and effects are not affected (use filter.remove / effect.remove). To reset only HSL or curves use segment.reset_hsl / segment.reset_curves.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Reset.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} without adjustments (an adjustment-layer segment keeps a neutral adjust object).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Straightens tone curves of a clip or adjustment segment: one channel (master, r, g or b) or all of them when channel is omitted — the reset button of CapCut's Curves page. Other adjustments are kept. Resetting straight curves is a no-op.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Curves/Reset.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} — segment.adjust.curves without the reset channel(s).

channel.description: Channel to straighten; omit to reset every channel and the preset.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Resets the HSL page of a clip's (or adjustment segment's) colour adjustments: one band back to h = s = l = 0, or every band when band is omitted or "all" — the reset button of CapCut's HSL page. Other adjustments (basic sliders, curves, LUT) are kept. Resetting bands that are already neutral is a no-op.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/HSL/Reset.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} — segment.adjust.hsl without the reset band(s).

band.description: Band to reset; omit (or "all") to reset all eight bands.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Sets colour/light controls of a video or photo clip, or of an adjustment segment (which applies to all tracks below it) — the Adjustment tab → Basic in CapCut. Pass any subset of: brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, vignette, hue (global hue rotation, -1..1 = -180°..+180°) and shine (local contrast / clarity; negative = soft glow) — each -1..1, 0 = neutral; CapCut's inspector shows them as -100..100 — and sharpen, fade (lifted blacks) and grain (film grain) 0..1, plus an optional .cube LUT with lut_intensity 0..1. Omitted fields keep their value. Fields animated by keyframes (adjust.<field>) record the value as a keyframe at the playhead. Render order: exposure → brightness → contrast → highlights/shadows → temperature/tint → hue + HSL → saturation → curves → fade → LUT → shine → sharpen → vignette → grain. Per-colour-range changes use segment.set_hsl, tone curves segment.set_curves, automatic correction adjustment.auto_enhance; segment.reset_adjust returns everything (incl. HSL and curves) to neutral.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Basic.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, keyframed?} with segment.adjust.

example5.summary: Crisper textures and a slight hue shift

fade.description: Fade: lifts the black point for a washed-out film look, 0 off … 1 strong (blacks become dark grey).

grain.description: Grain: film grain, 0 off … 1 heavy. Deterministic per picture (a still image never shimmers; video grain moves with the content).

highlights.description: Highlights: -1 recover bright areas … +1 boost them.

hue.description: Hue: rotates every colour around the colour wheel, -1 = -180° … +1 = +180° (0.1 ≈ 18°).

lut.description: Absolute path of a .cube LUT file to apply ("" removes the LUT). lut_intensity defaults to 1 when a LUT is first set.

lut_intensity.description: Strength of the LUT 0..1 (only used when lut is set).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

shadows.description: Shadows: -1 deepen dark areas … +1 lift them.

shine.description: Shine: local contrast / clarity, -1 soft and glowy … +1 crisp textures (unsharp mask with a large radius on luminance).

post.description:
Sets the sound processing options of an audio segment or video clip: voice_effect is a voice changer preset (Audio → Voice changer in CapCut; "" or "none" removes it): chipmunk, deep, monster, robot, pitch_up, pitch_down, whisper, echo, reverb, underwater, small_room, cathedral, stadium, megaphone, telephone, lofi, radio_am, walkie_talkie, bitcrush, vibrato, tremble, alien_ring, vocal_enhance, bass_boost, chorus_wide. reduce_noise toggles CapCut's Reduce noise, normalize_loudness toggles Normalize loudness (evens out the clip's perceived loudness). Only supplied fields change.
UI: Inspector/Audio.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with voice_effect / reduce_noise / normalize_loudness.

normalize_loudness.description: Normalise the clip to a standard loudness level.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

reduce_noise.description: Remove steady background noise (hiss, hum, wind).
