voice_effect.description: Voice changer id, e.g. "robot" or "chipmunk" (full list in the description; also library.list {kind: "voice_effect"}); "none" or "" removes the effect.

post.description:
Sets the canvas fill shown behind a main-track clip where it does not cover the frame (e.g. a vertical video on a 16:9 canvas) — Video → Basic → Canvas in CapCut. type: color (solid colour), blur (blurred, zoomed copy of the clip; blur 0..1 = strength), image (a picture file), none (use the project's canvas background from project.set_canvas). apply_to_all copies the setting to every video/photo clip on the main track (CapCut's 'Apply to all'). Only main-track clips have a canvas background.
UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Canvas.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, note?} — the selected segment after the change; note reports how many clips were updated by apply_to_all.

example1.summary: Blurred background behind a vertical clip

apply_to_all.description: Also apply to every other video/photo clip on the main track.

blur.description: Blur strength for type=blur: 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 match CapCut's four blur levels (default 0.5). Unit: fraction 0..1.

image.description: Absolute path of an image file for type=image.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

type.description: Fill type: color, blur, image, or none to fall back to the project background.

post.description:
Sets how a clip mixes with the layers below it — Video → Basic → Blend in CapCut. Blend modes only show a difference on overlay tracks (or text/stickers) because the main track has nothing below it except the canvas. Modes: normal, darken, screen, overlay, multiply, lighten, hard_light, soft_light, linear_burn, color_burn, color_dodge, add (linear dodge / lighter), difference, exclusion. Optionally sets opacity in the same call.
UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Blend.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, keyframed?}.

mode.description: Blend mode; normal resets to plain alpha compositing.

opacity.description: Optional opacity 0..1 (the slider in the same Blend section). Unit: fraction 0..1.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Removes a colour from a video/photo clip (green/blue screen) — Video → Remove BG → Chroma key in CapCut. color is the colour to key out (#RRGGBB, CapCut's colour picker); intensity 0..1 is how wide a range of similar colours becomes transparent (default 0.5 when the key is created); shadow 0..1 keeps/darkens shadows cast on the screen. enabled=false removes the chroma key. Usually applied to a clip on an overlay track above a background clip.
UI: Inspector/Video/Remove BG/Chroma key.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with segment.chroma_key (omitted when removed).

color.description: Key colour as #RRGGBB, e.g. "#00ff00" for a green screen. Required when creating the key.

enabled.description: false removes the chroma key (other parameters are then ignored).

intensity.description: How aggressively similar colours are removed: 0 = nothing, 1 = very wide range. Unit: fraction 0..1.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

shadow.description: Shadow strength kept from the keyed area: 0 = none. Unit: fraction 0..1.

post.description:
Crops a video or photo clip to a rectangle given in source fractions (0..1 of the original frame, before rotation/scale): x,y is the top-left corner of the kept area, w,h its size. The full frame {x:0,y:0,w:1,h:1} removes the crop. The rectangle must lie inside the frame (x+w ≤ 1, y+h ≤ 1). For ratio presets or resetting use timeline.segment.crop, which is what the toolbar Crop dialog calls.
UI: Toolbar/Crop.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with segment.crop set (omitted when the crop was removed).

h.description: Height of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (1 = full height). Unit: source fraction.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

w.description: Width of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (1 = full width). Unit: source fraction.

x.description: Left edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (0 = left edge). Unit: source fraction.

y.description: Top edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (0 = top edge). Unit: source fraction.

post.description:
Sets the tone curves of a video/photo clip or adjustment segment — the Curves page of CapCut's Adjustment tab. A curve maps input level x to output level y (both 0..1, 0 = black, 1 = white) through up to 16 control points joined by a smooth monotone cubic (no overshoot: rising points give a rising curve). The master (luma) curve applies to all channels first, then the r, g and b curves. Ways to call it: preset alone replaces every channel with a built-in look (lighten, darken, fade, contrast, cool, warm, vintage; custom = straight lines to edit by hand); channel + points replaces one channel (channel defaults to master); preset + channel + points starts from the preset and then replaces that channel. points is an array of [x, y] pairs or {x, y} objects; they are sorted by x, x values must differ, and the straight line [[0,0],[1,1]] means 'no change'. Examples of shapes: S-curve [[0,0],[0.25,0.18],[0.75,0.82],[1,1]] adds contrast; [[0,0.1],[1,1]] lifts the blacks (matte); a red curve [[0,0],[0.5,0.56],[1,1]] warms the midtones. Curves render after the basic sliders and HSL and before a .cube LUT.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Curves.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} — segment.adjust.curves {preset, master, r, g, b} (omitted when every channel is a straight line).

example2.summary: Gentle S-curve on the master channel

example3.summary: Cool the shadows: lift blue at the bottom

example4.summary: Fade preset with a warmer red channel

channel.description: Channel that points apply to: master (luma, all channels), r, g or b. Defaults to master.

points.description: Control points of the channel: 2..16 pairs [x, y] (or {x, y} objects), each 0..1. [[0,0],[1,1]] = identity (clears the channel).

preset.description: Built-in curve set: custom (straight lines), lighten, darken, fade, contrast, cool, warm or vintage. Replaces all four channels.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Sets the audio fade-in and fade-out lengths of an audio segment or video clip — Audio → Basic → Fade in / Fade out in CapCut. Each fade is clamped to half of the segment's timeline duration (the result reports the applied values in a note when clamping happened); 0 removes the fade. Only supplied fields change. Fades are re-clamped automatically when the segment gets shorter (speed change, trim).
UI: Inspector/Audio/Basic/Fade.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, note?} with segment.fade_in_us / fade_out_us.

example1.summary: 1 s fade in and 2 s fade out

fade_in_us.description: Fade-in length from silence at the segment start (0 = none). 1000000 = 1 second. Unit: microseconds.

fade_out_us.description: Fade-out length to silence at the segment end (0 = none). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Adjusts one colour range of a video/photo clip or adjustment segment — the HSL page of CapCut's Adjustment tab (8 colour dots). Bands: red (0°), orange (30°), yellow (60°), green (120°), cyan (180°), blue (240°), purple (270°), magenta (300°). Each band has h (hue shift: -1 = -30° … +1 = +30° around the colour wheel), s (saturation: -1 = grey, +1 = double) and l (lightness: -1 darker … +1 lighter), all -1..1 with 0 = unchanged. Pixels between two band centres belong to both with smooth weights, so there are no hard edges, and a band never affects hues beyond its neighbours (shifting red does not touch blue). Neutral greys are never changed. Omitted h/s/l keep their value. band "all" writes the given values into every band (e.g. s -1 → black and white). Alternatively pass bands = {red: {h, s, l}, …} to set several bands at once (omitted bands and fields are kept). Use segment.reset_hsl to clear one band or all of them. Typical recipes: bluer sky = blue {s: 0.3, l: -0.2}; greener foliage = yellow {h: 0.4} + green {s: 0.3}; skin = orange {s: -0.1, l: 0.1}.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/HSL.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} — segment.adjust.hsl holds all eight bands {h, s, l} (omitted when every band is neutral).

band.description: Colour band to change, or "all" for every band. Required unless bands is given.

bands.description: Several bands at once: {"blue": {"s": 0.3, "l": -0.2}, "orange": {"l": 0.1}}. Keys are band names, values objects with h/s/l (-1..1).

h.description: Hue shift of the band, -1..1 (= -30°..+30°; positive moves towards the next band, e.g. red → orange).

l.description: Lightness of the band, -1..1 (-1 = much darker, 0 = unchanged, +1 = much lighter).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

s.description: Saturation of the band, -1..1 (-1 = fully grey, 0 = unchanged, +1 = twice as saturated).

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Adds, edits or removes the mask of a video/photo clip — Video → Mask in CapCut. Shapes: linear (one straight edge through the centre, rotate it to choose the side), mirror (a band of height h), circle (ellipse w×h), rectangle (w×h with round corners), heart, star; none removes the mask. Geometry is in clip fractions: x,y is the centre (0.5,0.5 = middle of the clip), w,h the size (1 = clip size), rotation in degrees, feather 0..1 softens the edge, round 0..1 rounds rectangle corners, invert shows the outside instead. Changing the type resets the geometry to that shape's defaults; omitted fields keep their value. type may be omitted to tweak an existing mask.
UI: Inspector/Video/Mask.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with segment.mask (omitted when removed).

example2.summary: Split screen with a linear mask

feather.description: Edge softness: 0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft. Unit: fraction 0..1.

h.description: Mask height relative to the clip height (mirror band height, circle, rectangle, heart, star). Unit: clip fraction.

invert.description: Show the area outside the shape instead of inside.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

rotation.description: Rotation of the mask shape in degrees clockwise. Unit: degrees.

round.description: Corner roundness of the rectangle mask: 0 = square corners, 1 = pill shape. Unit: fraction 0..1.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

type.description: Mask shape; none removes the mask. Required when the clip has no mask yet.

w.description: Mask width relative to the clip width (circle, rectangle, heart, star). Unit: clip fraction.

x.description: Horizontal centre of the mask (0 = left edge of the clip, 0.5 = middle, 1 = right edge). Unit: clip fraction.

y.description: Vertical centre of the mask (0 = top edge of the clip, 0.5 = middle, 1 = bottom edge). Unit: clip fraction.

post.description:
Sets how opaque a visual segment is — Video → Basic → Blend → Opacity in CapCut (0 = invisible, 1 = fully opaque; the inspector shows 0..100%). Works for video, photo, sticker and text segments. If opacity is animated by keyframes the value is recorded as a keyframe at the playhead.
UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Blend/Opacity.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, keyframed?}.

opacity.description: Opacity: 0 = transparent, 0.5 = half see-through, 1 = opaque. Unit: fraction 0..1.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Changes the playback speed of a video clip or audio segment — Speed → Normal in CapCut (0.1x..100x). The source range stays the same and the timeline duration is recomputed: duration = source duration / speed (2x halves the clip, 0.5x doubles it). Any speed curve is removed. On the main track with the magnet on, the following clips ripple left/right to stay gapless (linked segments on other tracks move with them). On other tracks, slowing a clip down so it would overlap the next segment fails with conflict. Keyframes keep their position relative to the content; fades, animations and transitions are clamped to the new length. keep_pitch preserves the voice pitch (CapCut's Pitch toggle off = chipmunk effect).
UI: Inspector/Speed/Normal.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, rippled_segments?: number of other segments moved}. segment.target.duration_us is the new length.

example2.summary: Slow motion keeping the voice pitch

keep_pitch.description: Keep the original audio pitch when the speed is not 1 (omit to keep the current setting).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

speed.description: Playback speed: 1 = normal, 2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = slow motion. Unit: multiplier.

post.description:
Applies a variable speed curve to a video clip or audio segment — Speed → Curve in CapCut. Presets: montage (fast/slow alternating), hero (slow-motion moment in the middle), bullet (extreme bullet-time slowdown), jump_cut (sudden speed burst), flash_in (starts very fast), flash_out (ends very fast), custom (flat 1x curve to edit) and none (remove the curve, back to the normal speed in segment.speed). Instead of a preset you can pass points: 2..20 objects {x, y} where x is the position within the segment on the timeline (0..1, strictly increasing, first 0 and last 1) and y the speed multiplier there (0.1..100); speed is linear between points. The timeline duration becomes source duration / mean curve speed, with the same ripple/conflict rules as segment.set_speed.
UI: Inspector/Speed/Curve.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, rippled_segments?} — segment.speed_curve holds the points, segment.target.duration_us the new length.

example2.summary: Custom ramp from slow to fast

keep_pitch.description: Keep the original audio pitch while the speed varies.

points.description: Custom curve: array of {x, y} with x 0..1 (timeline position in the segment) and y the speed 0.1..100.

preset.description: Curve preset name; none removes the curve. Use custom with points for your own curve.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Sets position, scale, rotation and flips of a visual segment — Video → Basic → Transform in the CapCut inspector (also used for text and stickers). Only supplied fields change. Units: x and y move the centre of the clip in canvas fractions (0 = centred, 1 = centre on the right/bottom edge, -1 = left/top edge; positive y is down; range -2..2); scale is a multiplier where 1 = fit inside the canvas (0.01..4, i.e. 1%..400%); rotation is in degrees clockwise (-360..360). If a property is animated by keyframes, its new value is stored as a keyframe at the playhead instead (listed in result.keyframed), exactly like dragging a slider in CapCut after adding a keyframe. Audio, effect, filter and adjustment segments have no picture and are rejected with invalid_argument.
UI: Inspector/Video/Basic/Transform.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment: the updated segment, keyframed?: properties written as keyframes at the playhead}.

example1.summary: Picture-in-picture in the top-right corner at 40%

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees clockwise around the clip centre. Unit: degrees.

scale.description: Size relative to 'fit inside the canvas': 1 = 100%, 0.5 = 50%, 2 = 200%. Unit: multiplier.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

x.description: Horizontal offset of the clip centre: 0 = centred, 1 = centre on the right edge, -1 = on the left edge. Unit: canvas fractions.

y.description: Vertical offset of the clip centre: 0 = centred, 1 = centre on the bottom edge, -1 = on the top edge. Unit: canvas fractions.

post.description:
Sets the video clean-up of a video clip: 'Reduce image noise' (denoise) and 'Remove flicker' (deflicker) from the Basic section of CapCut's video inspector. Both are applied by the renderer while decoding the clip, so the preview, preview.frame and export all show them. denoise is a strength 0..1 (0 = off): up to 0.7 a fast spatio-temporal denoiser (ffmpeg hqdn3d) is used, above 0.7 a stronger but slower non-local-means denoiser (nlmeans) — expect slower previews/exports at high values. deflicker smooths frame-to-frame brightness changes (mains-light flicker, timelapse exposure jumps) with a 5-frame window. Only video clips are supported (photos have no frame-to-frame noise). Omitted parameters keep their current value; pass at least one. Undoable.
UI: Inspector/Video/Basic.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, denoise, deflicker, filter}: filter is the ffmpeg filter chain now used for the clip.

deflicker.description: true removes brightness flicker, false turns it off.

denoise.description: Noise reduction strength 0..1 (0 = off, 0.3 = light, 0.6 = strong, > 0.7 = very strong/slow).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Video clip to clean up (timeline.get lists segment ids).

post.description:
Sets the loudness of an audio segment or of a video clip's own sound — Audio → Basic → Volume in CapCut. volume_db is in decibels relative to the original: 0 = unchanged, -6 ≈ half as loud, +6 ≈ twice, -60 (the bottom of the slider) = muted, max +20. It is stored as linear gain in segment.volume (gain = 10^(dB/20)). If volume is animated by keyframes the value becomes a keyframe at the playhead. Photos, text, stickers, effects and filters have no sound and are rejected. Track-level mute is timeline.track.set {muted}.
UI: Inspector/Audio/Basic/Volume.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, keyframed?} — segment.volume holds the linear gain.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

volume_db.description: Gain in dB: 0 = original loudness, negative = quieter, positive = louder, -60 = mute. Unit: decibels.

post.description:
Adds a built-in sound effect to the timeline as an audio clip — the "+" button (or drag) of a sound effect in the Audio panel. The effect's WAV is synthesised once into the library folder (<DataDir>/library/sfx/<id>.wav), imported as a material named after the effect (the same material is reused when the effect is added again) and placed at at_us (default: the playhead) on the first audio track that is free for its whole length; a new audio track is created when all are busy (or next to track_id when that track is busy). The clip keeps the effect's full length; trim, fade or change its volume afterwards with the usual segment commands. Typical use: whoosh on a cut, pop when a sticker appears, ding on a key point, riser that ENDS at a drop (at_us = drop_us - duration_us).
UI: Library/Audio/Sound effects.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, track_id, material_id, sfx_id, name, start_us, duration_us}.

at_us.description: Timeline time where the effect starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: Audio track to place it on. Omit to use the first free audio track (or a new one).

post.description:
Lists Kadr's built-in sound effects (left panel → Audio → Sound effects), like CapCut's sound-effect library but entirely ORIGINAL: every effect is synthesised by the engine (no recordings). Categories: Popular, Transition (whooshes, swishes, risers, downlifter, glitch), UI (clicks, pops, ding, chimes, typing), Impact (booms, hits, punch, thud, metal, snare), Magic (sparkle, shimmer, chimes), Camera (shutter, flash, film), Countdown (tick, 3-2-1 beeps, buzzer), Cartoon & Game (boing, slide whistle, coin, laser, power-up, cash register) and Ambience (room tone, wind, pad, rain — quieter 6 s beds). Each item has an id for sfx.add, a name, categories, a description of how it sounds, its exact duration in µs, a 48-column waveform overview (peaks 0..1) and a preview path (GET it with the API token to play the WAV).
UI: Library/Audio/Sound effects.
Returns: {categories: [tab names in display order], total, items: [{id, name, category, categories, description, duration_us, channels, peak_db, peaks[48], preview, thumbnail}]}.

category.description: Only effects in this category (case-insensitive), e.g. "Transition", "Impact", "Popular". The result's categories lists all.

query.description: Case-insensitive search on id, name, category and description, e.g. "whoosh", "beep", "camera".

post.description:
Reports money spent on paid AI providers (cloud voices, video generation, AI assistant APIs) and the daily spending limits — Settings → Spending. Amounts are Kadr's estimates from each provider's published prices (estimated=true) or amounts the provider reported, recorded when a paid call or job was submitted (refunds of failed jobs are negative). Days are local calendar days; the limit resets at local midnight. today.total is in the limit currency (USD by default; other currencies are converted with limits.rates or built-in rates, the rest is listed under unconverted). Use it before starting paid work to see how much of today's limit is left.
UI: Settings/Spending.
Returns: {limits{daily (0 = none), currency, providers{id: daily}, rates?}, today{date, total, currency, providers{id: {amounts{currency: amount}, count}}, unconverted?}, remaining_today? (null without a limit), days[…same as today], entries[{time, provider, kind, model, op, amount, currency, estimated, job_id, note}]}.

example1.summary: How much did I spend this week?

days.description: How many days of history to return, newest first (1..400, default 7). Unit: days.

entries.description: How many individual charges to return, newest first (0..2000, default 50).

post.description:
Sets the daily spending limit for paid AI providers — Settings → Spending. Before a paid generation or cloud voice call Kadr reserves its estimated cost; if today's spending plus running jobs plus that estimate would exceed the limit, the call is refused (conflict error with a hint) instead of spending. daily is the limit for all providers together (0 removes it); provider + provider_daily set a separate limit for one provider id (the preset id, e.g. "fal", "elevenlabs", "runway"; 0 removes it). Calls whose cost is unknown are not blocked by the limit — the UI and the assistant still ask before running them. Omitted parameters keep their value. App setting, not undoable.
UI: Settings/Spending.
Returns: {limits{daily, currency, providers, rates}, today{date, total, currency, providers}, changed}.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the limit currency (USD, EUR, GBP, CNY…). Omit to keep it (default USD).

daily.description: Daily limit for all providers together in the limit currency; 0 = no limit. Omit to keep it. Unit: currency.

provider.description: Provider id for a per-provider limit (with provider_daily), e.g. "fal".

provider_daily.description: Daily limit for the given provider; 0 removes the per-provider limit. Unit: currency.

rates.description: Exchange rates as {currency: USD value of 1 unit}, e.g. {"CNY": 0.14}; merged into the stored rates.

post.x-user-only: Only the user changes the daily spending limit (Kadr's Settings → Spending).

post.description:
Adds a built-in sticker to a sticker track, like clicking a card in the Stickers tab. The sticker PNG (512×512, transparent, generated by the engine) is registered once per project as a material of type "sticker" and a segment using it is placed at at_us (default: playhead) for duration_us (default 3 s) on the first free sticker track, or a new sticker track above all visual tracks. The sticker starts centred at 30% of the canvas height (transform scale 0.3); move/resize it with segment.set_transform. Sticker ids come from library.list kind=sticker. Animated stickers (the "Animated" tab; their library item has params.loop_anim, optional params.in_anim and params.loop_us) get that loop animation (period loop_us) and entrance animation applied automatically, exactly as animation.set would; pass animate=false to place them still. Change or remove the animations later with animation.set / animation.remove.
UI: Library/Stickers.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, track_id, segment, material_id} — the sticker segment and the sticker material it uses.

example2.summary: Subscribe badge from 5 s for 2 s

example3.summary: Animated grin face placed without its default animation

animate.description: Apply the sticker's default loop/entrance animation when it has one (animated stickers only); false places it without animation.

at_us.description: Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

duration_us.description: Length of the new sticker segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

sticker_id.description: Sticker id from library.list kind=sticker, e.g. "heart", "badge_subscribe", "arrow_curved".

track_id.description: Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks.

post.description:
Adds a text segment to a text track, like clicking "Default text" or a text template in the Text tab. The segment starts at at_us (default: playhead) and lasts duration_us (default 3 s). Without track_id the first text track that is free over that range is used; if every text track is occupied (or none exists) a new text track is created above all other visual tracks so the text draws on top. Default look (CapCut "Default text"): white Go Sans, size 15 (font height ≈ 1/20 of the canvas height), centred, positioned in the middle of the frame (transform x=0, y=0, scale 1). template_id applies a text-template preset (library.list kind=text_template, may include glyph animations); style overrides individual TextStyle fields on top of the default or template — including the wave-2 fields (case, glow, fill gradient, extra_strokes, extrude, curve, glyph_in/out/loop, words, highlight). style.effect_id applies a word-art preset (library kind text_effect) first, so other style fields in the same object override it. Change the look later with text.update, move it with segment.set_transform.
UI: Library/Text/Default text.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, track_id, segment} — the new text segment (segment.text holds its TextStyle).

example2.summary: Title template at 2 s for 4 s

example4.summary: Gold word art that types itself

at_us.description: Timeline time where the new segment starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

duration_us.description: Length of the new text segment on the timeline. CapCut's default is 3 seconds (3000000). Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

style.description: Optional TextStyle overrides: {font, size, color, bold, italic, underline, align, line_spacing, letter_spacing, stroke{color,width}, shadow{color,opacity,blur,distance,angle}, box{color,opacity,radius}, case, glow{color,intensity,radius}, fill{type,colors,angle}, extra_strokes[{color,width}], extrude{color,depth,angle}, effect_id, curve, glyph_in/glyph_out/glyph_loop{id,duration_us}, words[{text,start_us,end_us}], highlight{style,color,scale,text_color}} — same units as text.update. Wave 4: stroke_fill{type,colors,angle,stops}, fill.stops[], pattern{type,colors,scale,angle,opacity,speed}, bevel{depth,angle,strength,gloss,highlight,shade,round}, inner_shadow{color,opacity,blur,distance,angle}, inner_glow{color,intensity,radius}, echo{colors,distance,angle,hollow}, distress{type,amount,scale}, sparkle{color,amount,size,speed}, drip{amount,length}, rough, pixelate, box{…, fill, border{color,width}, shadow{…}, per_line, skew, pad, knockout}, highlight.text_color.

template_id.description: Text template id from library.list kind=text_template, e.g. "title_bold", "neon_sign_pink", "gradient_pop_title".

text.description: Text content; use \n for line breaks. Defaults to the template's sample text or "Default text".

track_id.description: Put the segment on this existing track. Omit to use the first free track of the right type, or a new track created above all visual tracks.

post.description:
Applies a word-art preset ("text effect": gradient, metal, luxury, neon, candy, texture, sticker, hand-made, outline, 3D, retro, spooky, gaming and cute looks from library.list kind=text_effect) to a text segment, like clicking a card in the Text → Effects grid. The preset WRITES its fields into the TextStyle — fill gradient, glow, extra_strokes, extrude, the wave-4 pattern / bevel / inner shadow / inner glow / echo / distress / sparkle / drip / rough / pixelate fields and, where the preset uses them, stroke, shadow and color — after clearing the previous preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion, and records its id in effect_id. Rendering uses only the stored fields, so every value stays editable with text.update afterwards. Words, font, size, alignment, animations and timing are kept. effect_id "none" removes the preset's fill, glow, extra outlines and extrusion (a transparent hollow colour becomes white).
UI: Library/Text/Effects.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The new TextStyle of the segment.

effect_id.description: Text effect id from library.list kind=text_effect, e.g. "fx_gold_metal", "fx_neon_outline", "fx_3d_extrude", or "none" to remove.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Replaces the whole look of a text segment with a text-template preset (font, size, colours, stroke, shadow, box, spacing, glow, gradient, outlines, 3D, curve and the template's text animations) while keeping its words, timing, position, clip loop animation, caption word timings and any per-letter animation or highlight the template does not define — like clicking a template in the Text tab while a text clip is selected. Get template ids from library.list kind=text_template.
UI: Library/Text/Templates.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The new TextStyle of the segment.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Removes the per-letter / per-word text animation of a text segment from the in, out or loop slot (or all three with kind=all) — choosing "None" in the Text → Animate panel. Clip-level animations set with animation.set are not touched. Removing an empty slot changes nothing.
UI: Inspector/Text/Animate.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated TextStyle.

kind.description: Which slot to clear: in, out, loop or all.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Sets a per-letter / per-word text animation (library.list kind=text_animation) — the Text → Animate panel: typewriter with caret, letter rise/drop/pop/zoom/spin, karaoke sweep, random spell (scramble), word pop, word focus (blur-in), wave, jitter, rainbow, glow pulse, shine and more. These play INSIDE the text image and combine freely with each other and with the clip-level animations of animation.set. kind=in plays over duration_us from the segment start, kind=out over duration_us up to the segment end (in and out are shortened proportionally when they do not both fit), kind=loop repeats with duration_us as the period for the whole segment. A bare name is qualified with kind ("typewriter" + in → "in_typewriter"). Without duration_us the slot keeps its current duration, else the item's default_duration_us is used; in/out durations are clamped to the segment length.
UI: Inspector/Text/Animate.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated TextStyle (glyph_in / glyph_out / glyph_loop = {id, duration_us}).

example2.summary: Letters fall away at the end

duration_us.description: Duration of the in/out animation, or the period of one loop cycle (1 second = 1000000). Unit: microseconds.

id.description: Text animation id from library.list kind=text_animation (in_*, out_*, loop_*), e.g. "in_typewriter", "out_letter_drop", "loop_wave".

kind.description: Which slot: in (plays from the segment start), out (ends at the segment end) or loop (repeats for the whole segment).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Changes the content and look of a text segment — the Text tab of the inspector (Basic: font, size, style, colour, case, alignment, spacing; Stroke; Extra outlines; Shadow; Background box; Glow; Gradient fill; 3D extrude; Curve; Word-art effect; caption highlight). Only the parameters you pass change. Units: size is CapCut's scale (15 = default, font height ≈ size/300 of the canvas height); letter_spacing and line_spacing are in em (0.1 = 10% of the font size) added to the normal spacing; stroke_width, shadow_blur and shadow_distance are 0..1 (stroke up to 0.25 em thick, shadow offset/blur up to 0.5 em); shadow_angle, fill_angle and extrude_angle are in degrees counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right, -90 = downwards / top→bottom); box_radius 0..1 rounds the corners (1 = pill). Stroke, shadow, box, glow and extrude are enabled by setting any of their parameters (missing ones get defaults: black stroke width 0.3, black shadow opacity 0.6/blur 0.3/distance 0.15/angle -45, black box opacity 0.6/radius 0.2, glow in the text colour intensity 0.6/radius 0.35, dark-grey extrude depth 0.15/angle -45) and removed with stroke_width=0, shadow_opacity=0, box_opacity=0, glow_intensity=0 or extrude_depth=0. Gradient fill: fill_type linear|radial with 2–4 fill_colors (evenly spaced; radial goes centre→edge), fill_type=solid removes it (the text colour is used again); passing only fill_colors turns on a linear gradient. A color with alpha 00 ("#FFFFFF00") plus a stroke gives hollow outline text. curve -1..1 bends the lines into an arc (1 = half circle arch, -1 = smile). case upper|lower|title converts letters when rendering (the stored content is unchanged; none = as typed). effect_id applies a word-art preset from library.list kind=text_effect FIRST (it writes fill, glow, extra_strokes, extrude and the stroke/shadow/color it uses — the rendered look comes only from the stored fields), so other parameters in the same call override it; effect_id "" or "none" removes the preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion. Captions: words (timings relative to the segment start) plus highlight_style color|box|scale|underline|karaoke|pop|bounce|reveal|dim|glow|sweep_line|slide_box highlight the spoken word (highlight_style=none removes it). Per-letter animations are set with text.set_glyph_animation. Wave-4 word art (all optional; each group is enabled by any of its parameters and removed by its zero amount): fill_stops (hard-edged chrome/duotone gradients, up to 8 fill_colors); stroke_fill_* (gradient outline); pattern_* (procedural texture over the fill: stripes, checker, dots, halftone, hearts, stars, grain, glitter, holo, foil, brushed metal, marble, camo, galaxy, lava flow, aurora, rainbow…, pattern_speed animates the moving ones); bevel_* (emboss lighting; bevel_round + bevel_gloss = puffy glossy letters); inner_shadow_* and inner_glow_* (inside the letters); echo_* (stacked offset copies, retro 3D stacks / trails); distress_* (grunge, chalk, stamp, spray, scratch, worn); sparkle_* (star glints, sparkle_speed twinkles); drip_* (paint or slime drips); rough (hand-made wobble); pixelate (pixel-art blocks); box_* extras (gradient box, border, card shadow, one box per line, skew, padding, knockout stencil); highlight_text_color (letter colour of the active caption word). Highlight styles also include pop, bounce, reveal, dim, glow, sweep_line and slide_box.
UI: Inspector/Text.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated TextStyle object of the segment.
