align.description: Horizontal alignment of lines within the text block.

bevel_angle.description: Direction the bevel light comes from, counter-clockwise from the right (135 = upper left, the default). Unit: degrees.

bevel_depth.description: Bevel / emboss lighting: width of the lit edge 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes the bevel.

bevel_gloss.description: Sharp specular highlight on the bevel (glossy plastic / puffy balloon look) 0..1.

bevel_highlight.description: Bevel light colour #RRGGBB (default white; gold-ish for warm metal).

bevel_round.description: Rounded pillow profile (puffy, inflated letters) instead of a flat chisel.

bevel_strength.description: Contrast of the bevel light and shade 0..1 (default 0.8).

bold.description: Bold style (a real bold face when the font has one, otherwise synthesised).

box_border_color.description: Colour #RRGGBB of an outline drawn inside the edge of the background box.

box_border_width.description: Box outline thickness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes it.

box_color.description: Background box colour #RRGGBB. Enables the box if it was off.

box_fill_angle.description: Direction of the box gradient, counter-clockwise from the right. Unit: degrees.

box_fill_colors.description: 2–8 colours of a gradient background box (left→right unless box_fill_angle); [] removes the gradient. Enables the box if it was off.

box_knockout.description: Cut the letters out of the box so the video shows through them (stencil look).

box_opacity.description: Background box opacity 0..1; 0 removes the box.

box_pad.description: Extra padding around the text inside the box 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em).

box_per_line.description: One box per text line (ribbon / highlighter captions) instead of one box around the block.

box_radius.description: Corner roundness 0..1 (fraction of half the box height; 1 = pill).

box_shadow_angle.description: Box shadow direction, counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right). Unit: degrees.

box_shadow_color.description: Colour #RRGGBB of a drop shadow under the background box (blur 0 = flat offset "card" shadow).

box_skew.description: Slants the box into a parallelogram (-1..1; positive leans right) — sports and news lower thirds.

case.description: Letter case conversion at render time: upper (ABC), lower (abc), title (Abc Def) or none (as typed).

color.description: Text colour as #RRGGBB (or #RRGGBBAA; alpha 00 + a stroke = hollow text).

content.description: New text content; \n starts a new line. Must not be empty.

curve.description: Arc bend of every line: 0 = straight, 1 = half-circle arch (∩), -1 = half-circle smile (∪).

distress_amount.description: How much is eroded 0..1; 0 removes the distress.

distress_type.description: Erodes the whole text with a texture: grunge (rough print), chalk (chalkboard), stamp (rubber stamp), spray (speckled spray paint), scratch (scratched lines), worn (faded vintage print); none removes it.

drip_amount.description: Paint / slime drips hanging from the letters 0..1 (horror, slime, melting looks); 0 removes them.

echo_angle.description: Direction of the echo copies, counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right). Unit: degrees.

echo_colors.description: Echo: 1–6 colours #RRGGBB(AA) of offset copies of the letters stacked behind the text, nearest first (retro 70s/80s stacks, motion trails with fading alpha); [] removes the echo.

echo_distance.description: Distance between echo copies 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em); 0 removes the echo.

echo_hollow.description: Draw the echo copies as thin outlines instead of solid shapes.

effect_id.description: Word-art preset from library.list kind=text_effect (e.g. "fx_gold_metal", "fx_neon_outline"), applied before the other parameters; "" or "none" removes the preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion.

extra_strokes.description: Additional outlines OUTSIDE the main stroke, inner → outer, each {color:"#RRGGBB", width:0..1} (width like stroke_width); at most 4; [] removes them.

extrude_angle.description: Extrusion direction, counter-clockwise from the right: -45 = down-right (default), -90 = straight down. Unit: degrees.

extrude_color.description: 3D extrusion colour #RRGGBB (shaded darker with depth); #RRGGBBAA with alpha < FF draws a fading long shadow. Enables the extrusion if it was off.

extrude_depth.description: Extrusion depth 0..1 em; 0 removes it. Unit: em.

fill_angle.description: Direction of a linear gradient, counter-clockwise from the right: 0 = left→right, -90 = top→bottom, 90 = bottom→top. Unit: degrees.

fill_colors.description: 2–4 gradient colour stops #RRGGBB(AA), evenly spaced: first at the start (linear) or centre (radial), last at the end/edge.

fill_stops.description: Positions 0..1 of the fill_colors stops (one per colour, ascending; two equal neighbours make a hard edge such as a chrome horizon); [] = evenly spaced.

fill_type.description: Fill of the letters: solid (the text colour; removes a gradient), linear or radial gradient through fill_colors.

font.description: Font id from library.list kind=font (e.g. "go_sans", "go_mono", "sys_arial", or a downloaded font such as "montserrat" — install free fonts with font.catalog + font.install). Characters the font lacks (Cyrillic, CJK…) fall back to system fonts automatically.

glow_color.description: Glow (soft coloured halo) colour #RRGGBB. Enables the glow if it was off.

glow_intensity.description: How strong/opaque the glow is near the letters, 0..1; 0 removes the glow.

glow_radius.description: Glow size 0..1 (1 ≈ a halo reaching 1.3 em beyond the letters).

highlight_color.description: Highlight colour #RRGGBB (default #FFD600). Enables a color highlight if none was set.

highlight_scale.description: Growth of the active word for highlight_style=scale (default 1.15).

highlight_style.description: How the spoken word is highlighted when words are set: color (word turns highlight_color), box (rounded box behind it), scale (word grows), underline, karaoke (fills left→right as spoken), pop (springs up with an overshoot), bounce (hops once), reveal (later words hidden until spoken), dim (later words dimmed), glow (halo behind the word), sweep_line (underline grows while spoken), slide_box (box glides from word to word); none removes the highlight.

highlight_text_color.description: Colour #RRGGBB of the active word's letters for the box / slide_box / underline / sweep_line / glow highlight styles (e.g. black text on a yellow box); "" keeps the text colour.

inner_glow_color.description: Inner glow colour #RRGGBB: light seeping in from the letter edges (neon tube, lit-from-within). Enables it if it was off.

inner_glow_radius.description: How far the inner glow reaches into the letters 0..1 (1 = 0.3 em).

inner_shadow_angle.description: Inner shadow offset direction, counter-clockwise from the right (-60 = down, slightly right). Unit: degrees.

inner_shadow_color.description: Inner shadow colour #RRGGBB: a shadow cast INSIDE the letters (debossed / cut-out look). Enables it if it was off.

italic.description: Italic style (real italic face or a synthetic slant).

letter_spacing.description: Extra space between characters in em (0 = normal). Unit: em.

line_spacing.description: Extra space between lines in em (0 = normal, 0.5 = half a line more). Unit: em.

pattern_angle.description: Rotates the pattern from its default orientation. Unit: degrees.

pattern_colors.description: Pattern colours #RRGGBB(AA); their meaning depends on pattern_type (see its list); omitted = the type's defaults, "" = use the text fill.

pattern_opacity.description: How strongly the pattern covers the fill, 0..1 (0 = fully, same as 1).

pattern_scale.description: Pattern feature size multiplier (1 = default size relative to the font, 2 = twice as big; 0 = default).

pattern_speed.description: Animation speed of moving patterns (holo shimmer, glitter twinkle, flowing lava, rainbow sweep, scrolling stripes…), cycles per second; 0 = still.

pattern_type.description: Procedural texture painted over the letter fill: stripes (diagonal two-colour stripes (candy cane / barber pole); colors [stripe, gap] (gap defaults to the fill); speed scrolls them); pinstripe (thin vertical pinstripes over the fill; colors [line]); checker (checkerboard (racing flag); colors [a, b]); gingham (picnic gingham: translucent crossing bands, darker where they overlap; colors [band, background]); plaid (woven tartan with a twill texture; colors [main, dark band, secondary, thin accent]); dots (polka dots on a staggered grid; colors [dot, background]); halftone (comic halftone dots growing from the top to the bottom of the text; colors [dot] (default: a darker shade of the fill)); hearts (tiny repeating hearts (kawaii, love); colors [heart, background]); stars (tiny repeating five-point stars; colors [star, background]); grain (film grain / risograph noise that roughens flat colour; speed makes it flicker); static (black-and-white TV static noise; speed animates it); scanlines (dark horizontal CRT scanlines; speed rolls them); brushed (brushed-metal streaks along the pattern angle (shades the fill)); foil (crinkled metal foil facets of random brightness (gold leaf, tinsel); speed makes facets glint); carbon (woven carbon fibre; colors [dark, highlight]); glitter (glitter flakes of varying brightness with bright sparkles; colors [glitter] (default: the fill); speed twinkles); holo (holographic / iridescent pastel rainbow with a soft sheen; colors = palette (2–8); speed shimmers); rainbow (saturated rainbow bands; speed sweeps them across the letters); aurora (northern-lights curtains of green, teal and violet; colors = palette; speed drifts them); flow (flowing lava / fire plasma; colors = palette from dark to bright; speed makes it flow); galaxy (deep-space nebula with tiny stars; colors = palette; speed twinkles the stars); marble (polished marble with thin veins; colors [stone, vein] (stone defaults to the fill)); wood (wood grain rings; colors [light, dark]); camo (camouflage blobs in four colours; colors [1..4]); leopard (leopard rosettes; colors [fur, ring, spot centre] (fur defaults to the fill)); zebra (wavy zebra stripes; colors [stripe, background]); frost (frosted ice cracks and rime; colors [frost]); grid (glowing synthwave grid lines; colors [line]; speed scrolls the grid). none removes it.

pixelate.description: Blocky pixel-art rendering 0..1 (1 = 0.2 em pixels); 0 = smooth.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

rough.description: Hand-made wobble: shaky outlines and slightly tilted letters 0..1 (marker, crayon, doodle looks); 0 = clean.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

shadow_angle.description: Shadow direction, counter-clockwise from the right: -45 = down-right, 90 = up. Unit: degrees.

shadow_color.description: Shadow colour #RRGGBB. Enables the shadow if it was off.

size.description: Text size on CapCut's scale (default 15 ≈ 1/20 of the canvas height).

sparkle_amount.description: How many four-point star glints sit on the letters 0..1; 0 removes them.

sparkle_color.description: Colour of the star glints #RRGGBB (default white). Enables sparkles if they were off.

stroke_color.description: Outline colour #RRGGBB. Enables the stroke if it was off.

stroke_fill_angle.description: Direction of a linear stroke gradient, counter-clockwise from the right (0 = left→right, -90 = top→bottom). Unit: degrees.

stroke_fill_colors.description: 2–8 colour stops #RRGGBB(AA) of the stroke gradient; passing them alone turns on a linear stroke gradient (and a stroke if there was none).

stroke_fill_type.description: Gradient along the main stroke: linear or radial through stroke_fill_colors; solid removes it (stroke_color is used again).

stroke_width.description: Outline thickness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes the stroke.

words.description: Caption word timings [{text, start_us, end_us}] in microseconds relative to the segment start (normally written by captions.auto); matched in order onto the words of the text; [] removes them.

post.description:
Returns a compact view of the timeline made for AI agents — much smaller than project.get. Tracks are listed top-to-bottom exactly as the CapCut timeline shows them: text/sticker/effect/filter and overlay tracks first, then the main_video track, then audio tracks. Each track has its id, type, layer (its compositing index in project.tracks: 0 is drawn first, at the bottom), lock/hide/mute flags and its clips in time order. Each clip has id, kind (video, photo, audio, sticker, text, effect, filter, adjustment), label (file name, text content or effect/filter id), start_us, end_us, duration_us, the source range it uses, speed, volume (video/audio), link_group, transition_out, filter and effects. Also returns markers, the current playhead, the timeline settings and a compact list of materials with how often each is used. Call it before editing to find segment and track ids, and after editing to check the result.
UI: Timeline.
Returns: {project_id, name, duration_us, playhead_us, fps, settings, tracks: [{id, type, name?, layer, muted, locked, hidden, segments: [{id, kind, label, start_us, end_us, duration_us, material_id?, source_start_us, source_duration_us, speed, reverse?, still?, volume?, link_group?, transition_out?, filter?, effects?}]}], markers: [{id, time_us, label?, color?}], materials: [{id, type, name, duration_us, uses}]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Adds a marker on the timeline ruler at at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's marker button / M. Markers are labelled points used to remember spots (e.g. beats) and clip edges snap to them. If a marker already exists at exactly that time it is returned instead of adding a duplicate (its label/colour are updated when given).
UI: Toolbar/Marker. Hotkey: M.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

at_us.description: Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

color.description: Optional marker colour as #RRGGBB (default: the editor's accent colour).

label.description: Optional marker label (shown when hovering the marker).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Removes a marker from the ruler (right-click a marker → Delete in CapCut). Clips are not affected.
UI: Timeline/Ruler/Marker/Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {deleted: marker_id}.

marker_id.description: ID of the marker (from timeline.get → markers[].id or timeline.marker.add).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Moves a marker to another time on the ruler (dragging a marker in CapCut). Markers stay sorted by time; moving a marker never moves clips.
UI: Timeline/Ruler/Drag marker.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The moved marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

marker_id.description: ID of the marker (from timeline.get → markers[].id or timeline.marker.add).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

time_us.description: New marker time in microseconds. Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Changes the label and/or colour of a marker (CapCut's marker edit popover). Only the given fields change; an empty label clears it, an empty color returns to the default colour.
UI: Timeline/Ruler/Marker/Edit.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

color.description: New colour as #RRGGBB (empty string = default accent colour).

label.description: New label text (empty string clears it).

marker_id.description: ID of the marker (from timeline.get → markers[].id or timeline.marker.add).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Places an imported material (from media.import / media.list) on the timeline as a new clip — like pressing + on a media card or dragging it onto the timeline in CapCut. Where it goes: without track_id, video and photo clips go to the main track (created if needed); audio, sticker and other clips go to the first track of their type that is free at at_us, otherwise to a new track. On the main track with the magnet on (default) the clip is inserted at the clip boundary nearest to at_us and every later clip ripples right — there are never gaps; when at_us is omitted it is appended to the end of the main track. With the magnet off it lands at at_us and later clips are pushed right only if they would overlap. On other tracks the clip starts exactly at at_us (default: the playhead); if that spot on the requested track is taken, CapCut creates a new track directly above it and puts the clip there. new_track forces a brand-new track. Length: the whole material for video/audio (from source_start_us), 5 s for photos, 3 s for stickers; duration_us overrides it but cannot exceed the material for video/audio. Video clips keep their own sound until audio.extract. Locked tracks cannot receive clips (conflict).
UI: Library/Media/Card/+ (or drag to the timeline).
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — the track that received the clip and the full new segment (id, source and target ranges, defaults: speed 1, scale 1, opacity 1, volume 1).

example1.summary: Append a video to the end of the main track

example2.summary: Insert a clip at 5 s on the main track

example3.summary: Picture-in-picture: first 4 s of a video on a new overlay track at 2 s

at_us.description: Where the clip should start on the timeline. Default: end of the main track for video/photo going to the main track, the playhead for everything else. On the magnet main track the nearest clip boundary is used. Unit: microseconds.

duration_us.description: Clip length on the timeline. Default: the whole material (video/audio), 5000000 for photos, 3000000 for stickers. Unit: microseconds.

material_id.description: Material to place, e.g. "mat_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get ids from media.list or timeline.get → materials.

new_track.description: Put the clip on a brand-new track (an overlay track for video/photo) — next to track_id when given, otherwise at the default position on top.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

source_start_us.description: In-point inside the material for video/audio (the clip shows the material from this time on). Unit: microseconds.

track_id.description: Destination track. Must accept the material: video/photo → main_video or video_overlay, audio → audio, sticker → sticker. Omit to let the editor choose (see description).

post.description:
Crops a video or photo clip — the Crop button in the timeline toolbar, which opens CapCut's crop dialog with ratio presets. Rectangle fields are fractions of the source frame (x,y = top-left corner, w,h = size; omitted fields keep the current crop, or the full frame). ratio fits the rectangle to an aspect ratio of the source pixels: with no rectangle it picks the largest centred area of that ratio; with a rectangle it shrinks it around its centre to match. 'free' keeps the rectangle as given. Calling it with neither a rectangle nor a fixed ratio resets the crop to the full frame (CapCut's Reset). A legacy rect object {x,y,w,h} is also accepted.
UI: Toolbar/Crop.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with segment.crop set (omitted when the crop was reset).

example1.summary: Crop to a vertical 9:16 strip in the middle

h.description: Height of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (1 = full height). Unit: source fraction.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ratio.description: Aspect-ratio preset of the crop dialog. free = any shape.

rect.description: Alternative to x/y/w/h: an object {x, y, w, h} in 0..1 source fractions.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

w.description: Width of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (1 = full width). Unit: source fraction.

x.description: Left edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source width (0 = left edge). Unit: source fraction.

y.description: Top edge of the kept area as a fraction of the source height (0 = top edge). Unit: source fraction.

post.description:
Deletes clips from the timeline (the media stays in the library). On the main track with the magnet on the following clips shift left to close the gap (ripple delete); on other tracks a gap remains. Linked clips (e.g. a video and its extracted audio) are deleted together when linkage is on. Tracks other than the main track that become empty are removed, as in CapCut. The transition into a deleted clip is removed. Clips on locked tracks cannot be deleted.
UI: Toolbar/Delete. Hotkey: Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {deleted: [segment ids]} — every removed clip including linked ones.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the clip to delete. Required unless segment_ids is given.

segment_ids.description: Several segment ids at once (multi-selection). Combined with segment_id when both are given.

post.description:
Removes the part of a clip to the left of at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's "Delete left" (Q). On the main track with the magnet on the remaining part stays where the clip started and everything after it moves left, so the frame that was under the playhead is now at the clip's start (playhead_us; the editor moves the playhead there). Elsewhere the clip now starts at at_us. Linked clips are trimmed the same way. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.
UI: Toolbar/Delete left. Hotkey: Q.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment, playhead_us} — the shortened clip and the time the frame that was under the playhead now sits at.

example1.summary: Delete left of a clip at 3 s

example2.summary: Delete left at the playhead on the main track

at_us.description: Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected).

post.description:
Removes the part of a clip to the right of at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's "Delete right" (W). The clip now ends at at_us; on the main track with the magnet on the following clips move left to close the gap. Linked clips are trimmed the same way. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.
UI: Toolbar/Delete right. Hotkey: W.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment, playhead_us} — the shortened clip and the time the frame that was under the playhead now sits at.

example1.summary: Delete right of a clip at 3 s

example2.summary: Delete right at the playhead on the main track

at_us.description: Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected).

post.description:
Duplicates a clip with all its properties and places the copy directly after the original. On the main track the following clips ripple right (magnet) or are pushed right if they would overlap; on other tracks the copy goes right after the original when there is room, otherwise to a free or new track of the same type. Linked clips are duplicated too and the copies are linked to each other. The copy does not inherit the transition.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Duplicate. Hotkey: Ctrl+D.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — the new copy.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Freezes the video frame at at_us (default: the playhead) for 3 seconds — CapCut's Freeze button. The clip is split at at_us, a 3-second still image of that frame (a new segment with still: true, silent, keeping the clip's look: transform, crop, filters, adjustments, effects, mask) is inserted, and the rest of the clip plus everything after it on that track moves 3 s to the right (linked clips follow). Works on video clips only (not photos or freeze frames). Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used.
UI: Toolbar/Freeze.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — the new freeze-frame segment (3000000 µs long).

at_us.description: Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected).

post.description:
Mirrors a visual segment — the Mirror button in the timeline toolbar. Each call toggles the flip, so calling it twice restores the original. axis=horizontal (default) flips left↔right (Transform.flip_h); vertical flips upside down (flip_v). Use segment.set_transform {flip_h} to set an explicit state instead of toggling.
UI: Toolbar/Mirror.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with the toggled transform.flip_h / flip_v.

axis.description: Which flip to toggle: horizontal (mirror) or vertical (upside down).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Moves a clip to a new start time and/or another track — the same as dragging it in the CapCut timeline. On the main track with the magnet on, a move re-orders the clips: the clip is taken out (its gap closes) and re-inserted at the clip boundary nearest to start_us, so there are never gaps. On other tracks the clip starts exactly at start_us; if it would overlap another clip there, a new track is created directly above the destination track (below it for audio) and the clip goes there. Cross-track moves must respect the track type: video/photo between main_video and video_overlay tracks, audio between audio tracks, text/sticker/effect/filter only within their own type. Moving a clip off the main track closes its gap (magnet). Linked clips (link_group, e.g. video + extracted audio) move by the same amount when linkage is on; a linked clip on the magnet main track leads. Snapping (auto_snapping, 100 ms) aligns either edge with other clip edges, the playhead, markers or 0. Start times below 0 are clamped to 0. Clips on locked tracks, or a locked destination, give a conflict error. Tracks left empty by the move disappear.
UI: Timeline/Drag clip.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — where the clip ended up (start may differ from start_us because of the magnet or snapping).

example1.summary: Move a text clip to 10 s

example2.summary: Move a main-track clip onto an overlay track at 3 s

example3.summary: Re-order: put a main-track clip first

new_track.description: Create a new track for the clip next to track_id (or next to its current track): directly above for visual tracks, directly below for audio — like dropping a clip in the empty space between or above tracks.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

snap.description: Snap to the nearest clip edge, the playhead, a marker or 0 when within 100 ms (100000 µs). Defaults to the project's auto_snapping setting; pass false for an exact position.

start_us.description: New start time of the clip on the timeline. Omit to keep the current start (track change only). Unit: microseconds.

track_id.description: Destination track (must accept the clip type). With new_track: the track the new track is created next to. Omit to stay on the current track.

post.description:
Replaces the media of a clip while keeping its position, length, speed and every edit (filters, effects, adjustments, animations, keyframes, transitions, volume) — CapCut's "Replace clip". Video and photo clips accept video or photo materials, audio clips accept audio, stickers accept stickers. A video/audio replacement must be long enough: it needs duration × speed of source from source_start_us, otherwise invalid_argument explains how much is missing. The crop is reset because the new media may have another shape.
UI: Timeline/Context menu/Replace clip.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — the clip with its new material.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

source_start_us.description: In-point inside the new material (video/audio). Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Plays a video clip (or audio segment) backwards — the Reverse button in the timeline toolbar. The clip keeps its position, length and source range; only the playback direction flips (segment.reverse). Without the reverse parameter each call toggles; pass reverse=true/false to set it explicitly. Photos and freeze frames cannot be reversed.
UI: Toolbar/Reverse.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with segment.reverse.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

reverse.description: true = play backwards, false = forwards. Omit to toggle.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Rotates a visual segment by 90° — the Rotate button in the timeline toolbar. Clockwise by default; the result is normalised into -360..360 so four clicks return to 0°. For arbitrary angles use segment.set_transform {rotation}. If rotation is keyframed, the new angle becomes a keyframe at the playhead.
UI: Toolbar/Rotate.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment, keyframed?} with the new transform.rotation.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id or from timeline.get.

post.description:
Splits a clip into two at at_us (default: the playhead), exactly like CapCut's Split button / Ctrl+B. Both halves keep every property (transform, filters, effects, adjustments, volume, speed, mask…); the left half keeps the original id and the in-animation and fade-in, the right half gets a new id, the out-animation, fade-out and the transition to the next clip. Keyframes are divided at the cut with an interpolated keyframe on both sides so the motion does not change. Linked clips that span the same time are split too and the right halves stay linked to each other. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is split. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.
UI: Toolbar/Split. Hotkey: Ctrl+B.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, left, right, linked_right_ids?} — both halves (full segments) and the ids of linked right halves.

example2.summary: Split the main-track clip under the playhead

at_us.description: Timeline time in microseconds (1 s = 1000000). Defaults to the current playhead position. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit. Optional: when omitted the clip on the main track under at_us is used (what CapCut does when nothing is selected).

post.description:
Moves the left or right edge of a clip to to_us — like dragging a clip edge in CapCut — which changes which part of the source is used. Video and audio cannot be extended past the start or end of their media (the edge stops there); photos, freeze frames, text, stickers, effects and filters can be stretched freely. Speed is respected: at 2x one second on the timeline uses two seconds of source (source_duration = duration × speed). A clip is never shorter than one frame. On the main track with the magnet on, the clip keeps its start and every later clip ripples (trimming the left edge removes content from the beginning and pulls the rest left); elsewhere the edge cannot pass the neighbouring clip. Linked clips are trimmed by the same amount. Keyframes stay attached to the content, fades and animations are shortened if needed, and a transition is shortened to at most half of either neighbour. If the request was limited, clamped is true and the segment shows the actual result.
UI: Timeline/Drag clip edge.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment, clamped} — the trimmed clip and whether the edge was limited by the media length, a neighbour or the minimum length.

example1.summary: Cut the first second of a clip that starts at 0

example2.summary: Make a clip end at 8 s

edge.description: Which edge to move: left = the clip's start (in-point), right = its end (out-point).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the segment (clip) to edit, e.g. "seg_1a2b3c4d5e6f". Get it from timeline.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

snap.description: Snap to the nearest clip edge, the playhead, a marker or 0 when within 100 ms (100000 µs). Defaults to the project's auto_snapping setting; pass false for an exact position.

to_us.description: New timeline position of that edge (for the magnet main track: where the edge would be before the ripple). Unit: microseconds.

post.description:
Toggles the timeline helpers on the right of CapCut's timeline toolbar. main_track_magnet: the main track never has gaps — inserts ripple later clips right and deletes close gaps; turning it on closes existing gaps immediately. auto_snapping: dragged clip edges, trims and moves snap to clip edges, the playhead, markers and 0 within 100 ms. linkage: clips sharing a link_group (a video and its extracted audio) are selected, moved, trimmed, split and deleted together. preview_axis: the player previews the frame under the mouse while hovering the timeline. Only the given toggles change; all default to on except preview_axis.
UI: Toolbar/Right toggles (magnet, snapping, linkage, preview axis).
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The settings after the change {main_track_magnet, auto_snapping, linkage, preview_axis}.

auto_snapping.description: Snap clip edges to other edges, the playhead, markers and 0 (100 ms).

linkage.description: Edit linked clips (video + extracted audio) together.

main_track_magnet.description: Main-track magnet: keep the main track gap-free (ripple editing).

preview_axis.description: Preview the frame under the mouse while hovering the timeline.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Adds an empty track. CapCut usually creates tracks automatically when you drop clips (see timeline.segment.add and timeline.segment.move with new_track); use this when you want to target a fresh track explicitly. Position follows CapCut: video_overlay tracks go above the main/overlay tracks, text/sticker/effect/filter/adjustment tracks on top of all visual tracks, audio tracks below the existing audio tracks. A project has exactly one main_video track, so adding another one is a conflict. Note: tracks other than the main track disappear when an edit removes their last clip.
UI: Timeline/Track header.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The new track {id, type, name?, muted, locked, hidden, segments: []}.

name.description: Optional track name shown in the track header.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

type.description: Track type: main_video (only if missing), video_overlay (picture-in-picture), audio, text, sticker, effect, filter or adjustment.

post.description:
Deletes a track together with every clip on it. The main track cannot be deleted (delete its clips instead) and locked tracks must be unlocked first. Clips on other tracks that were linked to the removed clips stay where they are and lose their link.
UI: Timeline/Track header/Delete track.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {deleted_track: id, deleted_segments: [ids]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: ID of the track to delete (from timeline.get → tracks[].id).

post.description:
Changes the toggles in a track header: locked (clips on a locked track cannot be selected, moved, trimmed, split or deleted — every edit returns conflict until it is unlocked), hidden (the track is not drawn in the preview or export; visual tracks only), muted (the sound of every clip on the track is silenced; video and audio tracks) and the track name. Only the given fields change. Works on locked tracks so they can be unlocked.
UI: Timeline/Track header/Lock, Hide, Mute.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated track (with its segments).

hidden.description: Hide (true) or show (false) the track's picture in the preview and export.

locked.description: Lock (true) or unlock (false) the track against edits.

muted.description: Mute (true) or unmute (false) the sound of every clip on the track.

name.description: New track name; empty string clears it.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

track_id.description: ID of the track (from timeline.get → tracks[].id).

post.description:
Stops a running tools.install_ffmpeg download (the Cancel button under the progress bar). The partial file is deleted and the job ends in state "cancelled"; FFmpeg stays missing until tools.install_ffmpeg is called again. Does nothing (cancelled=false) when no download is running.
UI: First run/Cancel.
Returns: {cancelled: true when a running download was stopped}.

Downloads FFmpeg for Kadr — the first-run "Download now" button. Fetches the BtbN GPL build of FFmpeg 7.1 for Windows x64 (about 100 MB) from GitHub, verifies its SHA-256 against the checksums.sha256 file of the same release (a mismatch deletes the download and fails), then extracts ONLY ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kadr\tools\ffmpeg\bin where Kadr finds them immediately (no restart). Runs in the background and returns at once unless wait=true; progress arrives as tools.progress events (state downloading → verifying → extracting → done | failed | cancelled), or poll tools.status; stop it with tools.cancel. When FFmpeg is already available (PATH, next to Kadr, chosen folder) nothing is downloaded and already_installed=true, unless force=true. FFmpeg is licensed under the GPL (https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html). Only supported on Windows x64 (not_available elsewhere).
UI: First run/Download FFmpeg.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {started, already_installed, message, ...tools.status fields}.

force.description: Download Kadr's own copy even when an FFmpeg is already found (e.g. a broken or very old one on PATH).

source.description: Download source. Only "btbn" (github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, GPL build, FFmpeg 7.1 branch) is available.

wait.description: Block until the download is verified and installed (can take minutes) instead of returning immediately.

post.description:
Points Kadr at an FFmpeg that is already on this computer — "I have FFmpeg — choose folder". The folder (or its bin subfolder) must contain both ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe and ffmpeg must run ("-version"); it is saved as ffmpeg_dir in settings.json, used from now on (no restart) and on every start, and takes precedence over the copy next to Kadr, the downloaded copy and PATH. clear=true forgets the folder.
UI: First run/I have FFmpeg.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: The tools.status object after the change.

clear.description: Forget the chosen folder and go back to automatic lookup.

dir.description: Absolute folder path, e.g. "C:\\ffmpeg\\bin" or "C:\\ffmpeg" (its bin subfolder is checked too). Required unless clear is true.

post.description:
Reports whether FFmpeg and FFprobe — required for importing, previewing and exporting media — are available, where they were found (source: env = KADR_FFMPEG, custom_dir = folder chosen with tools.set_ffmpeg_dir, next_to_exe, downloaded = Kadr's tools folder, path = system PATH) and their version, plus the state of a running tools.install_ffmpeg download and where it would download from (source, license, approximate size). Kadr does not bundle FFmpeg; when ffmpeg.found is false call tools.install_ffmpeg (Windows x64) or tools.set_ffmpeg_dir.
UI: Settings/FFmpeg.
Returns: {ffmpeg{found, ffmpeg_path, ffprobe_path, version, source, error}, tools_dir, ffmpeg_dir, auto_download_supported, install{tool, state idle|downloading|verifying|extracting|done|failed|cancelled, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress, error}, source{id, name, url, checksums_url, page, license, license_url, approx_size_mb}}.

Removes the stored transcript of a material (e.g. before transcribing again in another language). Captions already created are kept. Undoable.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {material_id, words: number of words removed}.

material_id.description: Material whose transcript is removed (from media.list or transcript.get).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Finds a phrase in the transcript and cuts it out of the video — the easiest transcript edit for an AI agent ("delete 'so basically what I mean is'"). Matching ignores case and punctuation and is word by word within one clip. By default the first occurrence on the timeline is deleted (or the occurrence-th); all=true deletes every occurrence. The cut works like transcript.delete_words (split, delete, ripple, captions follow). One undo step; not_found when the phrase is not in the transcript.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {matches: total found, cuts: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us, text}], removed_us, captions_changed, duration_us}.

all.description: Delete every occurrence instead of one.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence to delete when all=false (1 = the first on the timeline).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ripple_captions.description: Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true.

segment_id.description: Only search this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip).

text.description: The words to delete, e.g. "you know what I mean".

post.description:
Transcript-based editing: deletes words from a clip by cutting the video/audio where they are spoken (select words in the transcript → Delete). ranges are inclusive word indices from transcript.get for that segment_id. Each range removes the time from the first word's start to the last word's end plus the silence after it (up to 0.5 s, so the next word follows naturally): the clip is split, the part is deleted together with linked clips (extracted audio), and the rest of the track moves left (on the magnet main track every later clip ripples, and linked clips follow). Caption cues follow the cut unless ripple_captions=false. Everything is ONE undo step. Word indices of the clip change after the edit — call transcript.get again.
UI: Library/Transcript/Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {cuts: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us, text}] (timeline times before the edit), removed_us, captions_changed, duration_us (project length after)}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ranges.description: Word ranges to delete: [{"from": 3, "to": 5}] (inclusive indices from transcript.get → words[].index). [3, 5] pairs and single indices are accepted too.

ripple_captions.description: Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true.

segment_id.description: Clip whose words are deleted (from transcript.get → segments[].segment_id).

post.description:
Returns the transcript of the timeline — the Transcript panel: for every clip with sound (main track, overlays, audio tracks; or only segment_id) the recognised words mapped onto the TIMELINE (speed, speed curves, reverse and trims are honoured; words outside the clip's trimmed range are left out), with their source times and confidence, plus the clip's text. Clips whose material has not been transcribed are listed with transcribed=false (run transcript.transcribe). Word indices are per clip and are what transcript.delete_words expects; they change when the clip is edited, so re-read after edits. Clips that are not heard (muted track, volume 0 — e.g. a video whose sound was extracted to a linked audio clip) are omitted unless include_silent=true.
UI: Library/Transcript.
Returns: {segments: [{segment_id, track_id, track_type, material_id, material_name, transcribed, audible, language, model, start_us, end_us, text, words: [{index, text, start_us, end_us (timeline), source_start_us, source_end_us, confidence}]}], count, words (total), untranscribed_material_ids}.

include_silent.description: Also list clips that are muted or have volume 0.

include_words.description: Include the word list (false = text only).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Only this clip (a video or audio clip).

post.description:
Cuts filler words out of the speech ("Remove filler words"): hesitation sounds that are always fillers — English um, uh, er, erm, ah, hmm, mm; Ukrainian/Russian е, еее, ем, ммм, а-а, хм, ну (elongated spellings like "ummm" match too) — and words often used as fillers only when they are set off by commas or sentence breaks: English like, you know, I mean, so, well, basically, actually, literally, kind of, sort of; Ukrainian типу, коротше, значить, ніби, як би, ну от, власне; Russian типа, короче, значит, как бы, вот, в общем. language=auto uses each transcript's language (all lists for other languages); words adds your own fillers (always removed). Each filler is cut like transcript.delete_words. Use preview=true to see the list first. One undo step.
UI: Library/Transcript/Remove filler words.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {found: [{segment_id, text, start_us, end_us}], count, removed_us, preview, cuts, captions_changed, duration_us}.

language.description: Built-in filler lists: auto (transcript language), all, none (only words), en, uk or ru.

preview.description: Only report what would be removed; the project is not changed.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ripple_captions.description: Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true.

segment_id.description: Only this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip).

words.description: Extra filler words or phrases to remove wherever they occur, e.g. ["okay", "right so"].

post.description:
Shortens every silence between words that lasts at least min_pause_us ("Remove pauses > X s"), using the word timings of the transcript: each pause is cut down to keep_us (half kept before, half after) so speech does not sound chopped. With edges=true the silence before the first and after the last word of a clip is trimmed too. Clips without any recognised words are left alone. Cuts ripple like transcript.delete_words; captions follow. Use preview=true to see the pauses first. One undo step. (For silence detection from the audio level instead of words see ai.remove_silence.)
UI: Library/Transcript/Remove pauses.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {found: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us}], count, removed_us, preview, cuts, captions_changed, duration_us}.

example2.summary: Tight edit: pauses over 0.5 s, keep 0.15 s

edges.description: Also trim the silence at the start and end of each clip.

keep_us.description: How much of each pause to keep (default 0.3 s). Unit: microseconds.

min_pause_us.description: Pauses at least this long are shortened (default 1 s). Unit: microseconds.

preview.description: Only report what would be removed; the project is not changed.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ripple_captions.description: Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true.

segment_id.description: Only this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip).

post.description:
Recognises the speech of one material (or of the materials of segment_ids, or of every audible clip when both are omitted) and stores it as the material's transcript: every word with its start/end in SOURCE time and a confidence. This is the Transcript panel's "Transcribe" button; no captions are created (use captions.auto or captions.from_transcript for that). Afterwards transcript.get shows the words on the timeline and transcript.delete_words / delete_text / remove_fillers / remove_pauses edit the video by editing the text. Materials that already have a transcript are skipped unless force=true or a different explicit language is requested. Runs as a background job like captions.auto (wait=true blocks). Not undoable (transcripts are analysis data; transcript.clear removes one).
UI: Library/Transcript/Transcribe.
Returns: Job status like captions.auto (kind "transcript"); when done result = {transcribed: [{material_id, language, model, words, text (first ~280 characters)}]}.

example2.summary: Transcribe everything on the timeline in English

device.description: Where recognition runs: auto (CUDA GPU when usable, else CPU int8), cuda or cpu. A failing GPU falls back to the CPU.

force.description: Transcribe again even when the material already has a transcript (e.g. to use a bigger model).

language.description: Spoken language: "auto" (detect, default) or a code/name such as en, uk, es, de, fr, pt, ru, zh, ja, ko, ar, hi, it, nl, pl, tr, vi, th, id, ms, bn, my, ro, tl (Filipino). Locales ("en-US") and English names ("Ukrainian") are accepted. captions.asr_status lists all ~100 languages.

material_id.description: Material to transcribe (from media.list). Omit to use segment_ids or every audible clip.

model.description: Whisper model size: tiny (fastest, least accurate), base, small (default: good accuracy, ~1× real time on a CPU, ~5× faster on an NVIDIA GPU), medium, large-v3 (best, slow without a GPU). Only models already downloaded can be used.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

prompt.description: Optional hint text for the recogniser: names, jargon or spelling to prefer (e.g. "Kadr, CapCut, Kyiv").

segment_id.description: Shortcut for a single clip.

segment_ids.description: Transcribe the materials of these clips.

wait.description: true = block until the job finishes and return its final status (with the result); false (default) = return the job right away and report progress through captions.progress events / captions.status.

post.description:
Puts the same transition between every pair of touching clips on a track (default: the main video track) — CapCut's "Apply to all" button. type/duration default to the transition of segment_id if given, else the first transition already on the track, else Mix 0.5 s. Each duration is clamped to half of the shorter clip of its pair; pairs with a gap or clips shorter than 0.2 s are skipped and counted. direction and softness work as in transition.set (they are applied on top of the copied type).
UI: Inspector/Transition/Apply to all.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, type, duration_us, applied: number of pairs set, skipped: number of pairs skipped}.

direction.description: Optional direction for transitions that have one (library item params.directions): the way the motion travels. For directional families (wipe_*, slide_*, push_*, cube_turn_*, whip_*) it selects the sibling id.

duration_us.description: Transition length; clamped per pair. See the description for the default. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Copy type and duration from this clip's transition (the selected transition in the UI).

softness.description: Optional edge softness 0..1 (0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft) for mask transitions with params.softness=true (wipes, irises, shape reveals, checkerboard, luma/ink dissolves, burns, light sweep).

track_id.description: Track to process (main or overlay video track). Defaults to the main video track.

type.description: Transition id from library.list kind=transition. See the description for the default.

post.description:
Describes the transition that follows a clip — what the Transition inspector shows when a transition badge is selected: the stored type, its library id and name, duration, the current direction and softness (defaults filled in) and which options the transition supports, plus the longest duration the pair allows. has_transition=false (and no transition fields) when the cut is a hard cut. Change it with transition.set.
UI: Inspector/Transition.
Returns: {segment_id, has_transition, next_segment_id?, max_duration_us?, type?, id?, name?, duration_us?, direction?, softness?, options?}.

example1.summary: Inspect the transition after a clip

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

post.description:
Removes the transition that follows a clip (segment.transition_out), turning it back into a hard cut. Removing from a clip without a transition is a no-op that reports removed=false.
UI: Inspector/Transition/Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.

post.description:
Adds or replaces the transition between a clip and the NEXT clip on the same track (main or overlay video track), like dropping a transition between two clips in CapCut. The transition is stored on the left clip (segment.transition_out) and plays across the cut. The two clips must touch (the next clip starts where this one ends, within half a frame); otherwise a conflict error explains how to fix it. duration_us is clamped to half of the shorter of the two clips (the result reports clamped=true); both clips must be at least 0.2 s long. Optional direction (left/right/up/down) and softness (0..1) apply to transitions whose library item lists them in params (directions, softness); they are stored in the type as URL-style options, e.g. "bars_stagger?direction=up&softness=0.3" (directional families such as wipe_left + direction up store the sibling id "wipe_up"; values equal to the defaults are dropped). Strip everything from "?" to get the library id. Asking a transition for an option it does not have is an invalid_argument error listing its options.

post.description:

post.description:

Many keys per provider are supported (e.g. ten ElevenLabs accounts): they are used in order and on quota / invalid / payment / rate-limit errors the next key takes over automatically. Pass one api_key, a batch (one key per line, "label: key" or NAME=value lines; blank lines, # comments and duplicates are skipped) or a file (.txt, .env, .csv, .json). Composite keys use the provider's key_format (AWS "ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET", iFlytek "APPID:APIKey:APISecret"). New keys are tested with a free request (test=false skips it) and providers needing a key become enabled. Keys are never returned — only masked previews like "sk_…a1b2". App setting, not undoable.

Risk: secret — handles credentials; only the user runs it (agents never send, read or change keys and passwords).

post.description:
Asks GitHub whether a newer Kadr is published — Settings → Updates → "Check now" and Menu → "Check for updates…". Downloads latest.json (+ latest.json.sig) from the release repository (stable: the latest regular release; beta: the newest release including pre-releases, via the GitHub API), verifies its Ed25519 signature with the key built into Kadr and compares versions with semver rules (1.1.0-beta.1 < 1.1.0-rc.1 < 1.1.0). Nothing is downloaded or installed. The release channel is PRIVATE (Kadr is distributed by invitation): without an access token, or with a token that cannot read the repository, the check succeeds with private=true, access="none", available=false and a reason ("ask the vendor for the latest installer"), the updater state becomes no_access and no event is published; save a GitHub token with update.settings {github_token} (or set KADR_UPDATE_TOKEN) to receive updates automatically. available=true means a newer version exists; skipped=true means the user chose "Skip this version" for it (it is still reported here but never announced automatically); can_install=false (with reason) means this build cannot self-update — portable builds, development builds without a signing key, or a release without a Windows installer — so open release_url instead. A pre-release is never offered on the stable channel. Publishes update.available when a newer, not skipped version is found. Fails with not_available when GitHub cannot be reached, not_found when the repository has no release yet, and internal when the signature does not verify (the update is refused).
UI: Menu/Check for updates….
Returns: {current, latest, available, channel, prerelease, notes_markdown, notes_url, release_url, published_at, size (installer bytes), installer, signed, skipped, required (current is older than min_supported), min_supported, portable, can_install, reason, checked_at, private (no access to the private channel), access public|token|none}.

channel.description: Release channel to look at: "stable" = regular releases only (the GitHub "latest" release), "beta" = also pre-releases such as 0.2.0-beta.1. Omit to use the channel saved in settings (update.settings).

post.description:
Downloads the installer of the newest version found by update.check (runs a check first when none was done in this session) into %TEMP%\Kadr-update\ and verifies its exact size and SHA-256 against the signed latest.json; a file that does not match is deleted and the update is refused. Runs in the background and returns immediately (state "downloading") unless wait=true; progress arrives as update.progress events, completion as update.ready, errors as update.failed. An installer already downloaded and verified is reused. Does not install anything — call update.install afterwards. Refused with not_available for portable builds, development builds without a signing key and releases without a Windows installer (open release_url instead), and with conflict when Kadr is already up to date.
UI: Settings/Updates/Download & install.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: The update.status object (state downloading, ready or failed).

wait.description: Block until the download finished and was verified (can take minutes for ~100 MB) instead of returning at once.

post.description:
Installs the newest version and restarts Kadr — the "Download & install" button. Downloads and verifies the installer first if update.download has not finished (SHA-256 + size from the Ed25519-signed latest.json, checked again right before running), then starts it detached with /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /CLOSEAPPLICATIONS /RELAUNCH and closes the desktop app about a second later. The installer upgrades in place, keeps all projects and settings, closes running Kadr processes (Kadr.exe, kadr-server.exe, kadr-mcp.exe) and starts Kadr again when done, so API clients lose their connection for a minute. UNSAVED WORK: projects are saved after every command, but running exports are cancelled. Requires confirm=true as a safety check. In the headless server nothing quits by itself: the result asks to exit. Refused for portable builds and builds without a signing key (not_available).
UI: Settings/Updates/Download & install.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.
Returns: {started, version, installer, args (the exact installer arguments), quitting (the app exits shortly), message}.

post.description:
Reads or changes the updater preferences stored in <data dir>/settings.json (key "update"). Without arguments it only returns them. auto_check (default on) makes Kadr check GitHub in the background after startup, at most once every 24 hours, never blocking the editor (a private channel without access stays silent); channel picks stable releases or also beta pre-releases. Regular builds such as 1.0.0 use the stable channel; builds that are themselves pre-releases default to beta. github_token stores the GitHub access token the vendor gave you for the private release channel (a fine-grained token with read-only Contents access to the release repository, or a classic token with repo scope); it is stored encrypted in Kadr's secret vault (Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain; Linux: a 0600 file — namespace "update", name "github_token", never in settings.json; a token an older version left in settings.json is moved into the vault on start), used only for requests to the GitHub API, and NEVER returned — results only show github_token_set and github_token_source (env = the KADR_UPDATE_TOKEN environment variable, which wins over the saved one; settings = saved with this command). Pass "" to remove it. AI agents never pass github_token (the built-in assistant refuses calls that carry credentials). Changing settings does not check by itself — call update.check afterwards.
UI: Settings/Updates.
Risk: system — changes the Kadr installation or this computer's setup; confirm with the user first.

Stops a queued or running generation: Kadr stops waiting and asks the provider to cancel when it can (fal, Runway, Replicate, BytePlus, DashScope, Higgsfield, Eachlabs…). Plans a video generation without running it: resolves provider/model, fills duration from the target range and aspect ratio from the canvas (auto_params), checks references and capabilities, picks the endpoint (text, image, first+last frame, references, video edit) and estimates the cost from the provider's published prices (dated; known=false when the provider bills credits or has no public price). Also reports today's spending against the daily limit (limit.over = generate would be refused by the overall or per-provider daily limit, with the estimate converted into the limit currency), whether a key is configured, and cached=true when an identical request already has a result (generate then reuses it for free unless new_take). post.description:
Starts an AI video generation job and returns at once (job_id); the job runs in the background: references are extracted (current frame, clip frames with FFmpeg) and uploaded, the provider is called with key failover, progress is published as videogen.job events, the video is downloaded to Kadr's results cache and — with a range or segment_id — placed into the timeline as one undo step. PAID: when the operation is billable, confirm_token from videogen.estimate is REQUIRED (the user must have agreed to the shown cost) and the daily spending limit is enforced. Agent workflow to fill a gap: videogen.providers (configured_only) → videogen.models {provider} → timeline.get (find the gap) → videogen.estimate {provider, model, prompt, project_id, start_us, duration_us, use_neighbors?} → ask the user → videogen.generate with the same arguments + confirm_token → poll videogen.job until state succeeded/failed (or wait for events); a succeeded job already carries placed (or place_error when the range could not be used), so do not place it again. Identical earlier requests reuse their result for free (new_take forces a new generation). Failures carry the provider's reason and a hint; retry with retry_of and changed arguments.

Risk: paid — spends money at a cloud provider; show the user the estimated cost and run it only after they agree (estimate → confirm_token).

Returns one generation job: state, progress (0..1, -1 when the provider does not report it), provider status message, error with hint, cost charged, references used, the result file (path, duration, size, url = API path that plays it) and the placement. Poll it (every few seconds) after videogen.generate until state is succeeded, failed or canceled. While the provider is unreachable the job stays unfinished with lost_contact_at and next_check_at (Kadr keeps checking, nothing is charged again); a failed job with resumable=true can be picked up with videogen.resume.

Deletes finished generation jobs from the history (the Generate panel's Jobs list) and, by default, their result videos from Kadr's results cache (<DataDir>/videogen/results) with their poster frames — to free disk space after many takes. Copies already placed on a timeline or imported into Media live in the project folder (<project>/ai-video) and are never touched, so projects keep playing; the spending ledger keeps its entries. A result file another remaining job still uses (the free reuse of an identical request) is kept. Queued or running jobs are refused (cancel them with videogen.cancel first). A failed job with resumable=true may still finish at the provider: after deleting it Kadr can no longer fetch that paid result. All or nothing: an unknown or unfinished id fails the call before anything is removed. Cannot be undone.

post.description:
Stores API keys for a video provider in Kadr's OS-encrypted vault (pool kind "video") — Settings → Video generation → Keys. Paste many at once (one per line, "label: key" or tab-separated, # comments ignored) or import a file (.txt/.env/.csv/.json; a Google service-account .json for Vertex AI). Keys are used in order with automatic failover: on 401/invalid the key is marked invalid, on quota/credits (402) exhausted, on 429 rate_limited, and the next key is tried; a running job always uses the key that started it. Composite keys go in one entry: Kling "ACCESS_KEY:SECRET_KEY", Higgsfield "KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET", Tencent "SecretId:SecretKey". post.description:
Lists video models with everything needed to build a request: capabilities (text_to_video, image_to_video, first_last_frame, reference_images/video/audio, video_to_video, audio = generates sound), tasks, and the parameter schema (name, type, enum values, min/max, default, unit — duration params have unit seconds — and file params with their role and accepted types). price_hint is the estimated cost of the default settings (prices are dated estimates from the vendor's page). Without provider it searches every provider (e.g. family "Seedance" or "Kling" to compare where a model is offered; providers with keys first). Use the ids and param names exactly in videogen.estimate / videogen.generate. Aggregators also expose their full catalogs (fal ~290, WaveSpeed ~350, Eachlabs ~270 endpoints…) imported from their published schemas: featured=false marks those; experimental ones had no per-model schema, so only common fields are sent (add others with extra_json). Results are paged (limit, offset, total).

post.description:
Imports a generated video (job_id, or any video file by path) into the project's Media (copied into the project folder) and places it — one undo step. With start_us + duration_us it fills that range: on the main track when the range is free there (with the magnet on it goes to the nearest clip boundary and later clips move right), otherwise on the first free overlay track or a new one (track_id forces a track). With segment_id it replaces that clip's media keeping its position, effects, transform and keyframes. fit: trim (speed 1, cut to the range), fit (speed changed so the whole clip fills the range, pitch kept), keep_speed (full length, may extend past the range), auto (trim when longer, fit when at most 20% shorter, else trim and leave the rest empty). import_only just adds it to Media. The same result can be placed many times.
UI: Generate/Place.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {material_id, material_path, segment_id, track_id, start_us, duration_us, speed, fit (trim|fit|keep_speed|none), generated_duration_us, replaced, note}.

post.description:
Adds a custom AI video provider — Settings → Video generation → Custom. Three ways: (1) simple fields for the usual async API (base_url, auth_style, submit_url + submit_body template, job_id_path, poll_url with {job_id}, status_path, video_path, optional progress/error/cancel/result) or mode "sync" when the submit response already holds the video; (2) clone a built-in preset and change its base_url (self-hosted proxies, regional endpoints); (3) a full preset object with every request template. post.description:
Lists the AI video generation providers Kadr can use — Settings → Video generation and the Generate panel. Built-in presets cover direct APIs (Google Gemini API and Vertex AI for Veo 3.1 / Gemini Omni Flash, Runway, Kling, Luma Ray, MiniMax Hailuo, ByteDance Seedance via BytePlus/Volcengine, Alibaba Wan via DashScope, Vidu, PixVerse, Pika, Higgsfield, Lightricks LTX, xAI Grok Imagine, Tencent Hunyuan) and aggregators (fal.ai, Replicate, WaveSpeed, OpenRouter, Kie.ai, PiAPI, GoAPI, AI/ML API, Segmind, Novita, Together, Runware, SiliconFlow, ModelsLab, Eachlabs, Atlas Cloud, DeepInfra), plus custom providers. configured = it has a usable key and every required setting, so it can generate now; keys are counted by status (ok, exhausted, invalid, rate_limited) but never shown. Each entry says what key to paste (key_hint), where to get it (keys_url) and when the preset was checked against the vendor's docs (verified_from_docs, verified_at). Retired providers (OpenAI Sora 2 shut down 2026-09-24, Stability's video API) are hidden unless include_retired.
UI: Settings/Video generation.
Returns: {providers: [{id, name, description, builtin, custom, aggregator, experimental, retired, configured, needs_key, key_hint, keys {count, usable, statuses}, settings [{name, type, doc, value}], missing_settings, default_model, models, featured_models, families, capabilities, docs_url, keys_url, pricing_url, verified_from_docs, verified_at, notes, is_default}], default: {provider, model}|null}.

post.description:
Follows a generation job the provider already accepted again, without submitting or paying for it again. Kadr keeps paid jobs through outages by itself (network down, laptop asleep, provider 5xx/429): the job stays queued/running with lost_contact_at, next_check_at and a "lost contact … checking again" message, and is checked with a growing pause (30 s up to 10 min) for up to 24 h after submission; unfinished jobs also resume automatically when Kadr starts. Call videogen.resume to check such a job right now, or to pick up a job that failed on Kadr's side (resumable=true: still unreachable after that deadline, its key or custom provider was missing, the download or disk failed) once the cause is fixed — the charge was kept for it because the provider may still bill it. Jobs the provider reported as failed, canceled or finished jobs, and jobs that never reached the provider are refused with a hint (use videogen.generate with retry_of for a new, paid take).
UI: Generate/Resume.
Returns: Job (see videogen.generate) — queued/running/downloading again with a "checking with … again" message; follow it with videogen.job or videogen.job events.

example1.summary: Check a job that lost contact again

post.description: Runs project commands in order on one project. If any call fails nothing is saved. All calls form a single undo step. With dry_run=true the result is computed and returned but not saved.
